nfl.off_epa.label: Offensive EPA/play, opponent-adjusted, recency-weighted
nfl.off_epa.mechanism: Per-play expected-points added measures how much each snap moves scoring expectation; adjusting for defenses faced isolates the offense's own repeatable efficiency, which drives points per drive and therefore margin and totals.
nfl.off_epa.rationale: EPA/play is the best single public descriptor of offensive efficiency and predicts future points better than points or yards, but it is noisy early in the season (~17 games) and dominated by QB and a few explosive plays. Naive averages double-count weak schedules; the subtle part is separating QB-driven from scheme/OL-driven EPA when the QB changes.
nfl.off_epa.measurement: From play_by_play (pass/run, no kneels/spikes, win-prob 5-95% filter optional): team offense EPA/play by game. Opponent-adjust with a ridge regression (offense effect + defense effect + home + intercept) fitted on rolling windows; exponential recency decay (half-life ~6-8 games) blended with a prior from last season regressed ~35-50% toward league mean, weight on prior shrinking with games played. Compute separately for pass (per dropback) and rush, and condition on the QB actually starting.

nfl.def_epa.label: Defensive EPA/play allowed, opponent-adjusted
nfl.def_epa.mechanism: Defensive EPA/play allowed is the opponent-adjusted rate at which a defense prevents expected points; it sets the baseline for what any offense (and any individual passer/rusher/receiver) will achieve against it.
nfl.def_epa.rationale: Defense is less stable than offense year to year and more sensitive to injuries to a few pass rushers/corners, so season-long averages lag true current strength; split pass versus rush defense because the two have different stabilization speeds and different relevance to QB versus RB markets.
nfl.def_epa.measurement: Same ridge adjusted-EPA framework as offense but on the defensive effect, split into pass EPA/dropback allowed and rush EPA/rush allowed. Recency-weight and shrink toward a preseason prior built from returning defensive snaps and last-year ratings. Re-weight for current injury-absent lineup using snap-weighted player contributions when available.

nfl.success_rate.label: Success rate and early-down efficiency
nfl.success_rate.mechanism: Success rate (share of plays with positive EPA, early-down emphasis) measures consistency of staying on schedule, which controls drive sustainment and penalizes explosive-play dependence.
nfl.success_rate.rationale: Offenses that lean on explosive plays have high EPA but low success rate and are volatile; success rate is more stable and complements EPA for totals and team totals because sustained drives shape plays per game and clock. It is also less sensitive to a single long TD.
nfl.success_rate.measurement: Per game: share of plays with EPA>0 on 1st/2nd down, and separately third-down conversion over expected given distance. Opponent-adjust with the same ridge approach; recency-weight; report the gap between EPA rank and success-rate rank as an explosiveness-dependence flag.

nfl.ratings.label: Power ratings and market-implied team strength history
nfl.ratings.mechanism: Closing lines embed injury news, weather and sharp information; the rating implied by spread history is the strongest prior on team quality and encodes information not visible in box scores.
nfl.ratings.rationale: Any model of NFL results must beat or at least calibrate against market-implied strength; the real use is as a prior or control so residual inputs add information instead of re-deriving what the line already contains. Subtle: lines move for QB/injury news, so ratings must be keyed to the lineup the line assumed, not the season average.
nfl.ratings.measurement: Invert historical spreads/totals/moneylines (games.csv) into team ratings via a Bradley-Terry/ridge fit per season with home edge; also keep Elo-style margin-based rating with MOV cap, QB adjustment (value of starter versus replacement), and 17-game season reversion (~1/3 toward mean). Track the rating at kickoff and the opening-to-close change.

nfl.roster_continuity.label: Offseason roster turnover, returning production and age curve
nfl.roster_continuity.mechanism: Share of last year's snaps and production that returns (and the age profile of the core) determines how much last year's ratings carry into this year, which dominates season-level markets and early-season game priors.
nfl.roster_continuity.rationale: Early-season game markets and season win totals depend on how much to trust last season; free agency, retirements, coordinator departures and aging curves create predictable regression. The subtle part is weighting by position value: QB and OL/pass rush turnover matters more than WR3 turnover.
nfl.roster_continuity.measurement: From rosters and snap_counts compute returning snap share by unit (QB, OL, DL/EDGE, secondary, skill) and value-weight by position (QB highest). Add age-weighted aging curve by position and expected improvement of young starters (years 2-3). Regress prior-season rating toward mean with shrinkage coefficient fitted on rolling train years as a function of returning share.

nfl.rush_efficiency.label: Rush efficiency, yards before contact and run-block quality
nfl.rush_efficiency.mechanism: Team rushing success depends on the OL run-block, scheme (zone/gap), box counts faced, and RB creation; yards before contact separate line/scheme production from back creation.
nfl.rush_efficiency.rationale: Rushing yards props and team rush totals need volume (script) times yards per carry; YPC is noisy and heavily driven by a few long runs, while rush EPA, success rate and yards before contact are more stable and attribute credit between OL and RB.
nfl.rush_efficiency.measurement: From play_by_play and PFR/NGS rushing: rush success rate, EPA/rush, yards before contact per attempt, yards after contact per attempt, stuff rate and explosive-run rate (10+). Opponent-adjust versus defense rush EPA allowed and box counts; recency-weight and shrink individual RB values toward team level.

nfl.pass_efficiency.label: Team pass efficiency: EPA/dropback, ANY/A, CPOE, air-yards profile
nfl.pass_efficiency.mechanism: Passing efficiency combines QB accuracy and decision-making, receiver quality, protection and scheme; it drives passing yards, TDs and scoring.
nfl.pass_efficiency.rationale: ANY/A and EPA/dropback bundle sacks and interceptions, while CPOE and air yards isolate accuracy and aggressiveness; combining them with opponent pass-defense quality gives expected efficiency for yardage and TD props. Early-season values need heavy shrinkage.
nfl.pass_efficiency.measurement: From play_by_play: EPA/dropback, ANY/A, completion % over expected (CPOE), average depth of target (aDOT), air-yards per attempt, sack rate, INT rate, YAC share. Opponent-adjust with ridge using opposing pass-defense factors; for a specific QB use career-weighted prior (more weight on prior when <300 dropbacks) and recent 6-8 game window.

nfl.qb_efficiency.label: QB-specific efficiency prior (EPA+CPOE, career-regressed)
nfl.qb_efficiency.mechanism: The starting QB explains the largest share of team offensive variance; a QB-level efficiency prior built from career and recent play predicts passing production beyond team averages.
nfl.qb_efficiency.rationale: Teams change QBs often (injury, benching), so team-level stats misprice backups and returning starters; career-regressed estimates avoid overreacting to 3-game hot streaks, while recency captures real changes in health, supporting cast and scheme. Rookies and journeymen need position-appropriate priors (draft slot, college efficiency).
nfl.qb_efficiency.measurement: Per QB: EPA/dropback, CPOE, sack rate, INT rate, designed/scramble rush EPA, computed from play_by_play with opponent and receiver-quality adjustment; Bayesian shrinkage with prior weight ~200-300 dropbacks centered on a draft-slot/experience-based mean; blend with last-8-game window. Flag small samples.

nfl.explosive.label: Explosive-play rate and chunk-yard dependence
nfl.explosive.mechanism: Offense/defense explosive-play rates (20+ pass, 10+ run) shape scoring variance and drive length; explosive-heavy teams score fast with fewer plays.
nfl.explosive.rationale: Explosiveness is partly skill (vertical passing game, speed) and partly luck; it matters for totals variance, for tail outcomes (long TDs for yardage-ladder tails) and for first-TD timing. Defensive explosives allowed regress strongly.
nfl.explosive.measurement: Share of offensive plays gaining 10+ rushing/20+ passing, opponent-adjusted; and the same rate allowed. Compute expected explosive rate from air yards/depth profile and separate persistent skill (aDOT, speed receivers) from residual luck; shrink residuals toward zero.

nfl.redzone.label: Red-zone and goal-to-go TD conversion
nfl.redzone.mechanism: Finishing drives (TD versus FG) turns yards into points; red-zone TD rate has a skill component (scheme, goal-line personnel, QB mobility) and a large luck component.
nfl.redzone.rationale: Points per drive is the final link from yardage to scoring: teams with high yard efficiency but low red-zone TD rate are expected to regress upward in points, and vice versa. Separating persistent red-zone play-calling from noise protects against chasing outliers.
nfl.redzone.measurement: Red-zone (inside 20) and goal-to-go TD rate, success rate and pass/run split, opponent-adjusted. Shrink toward league average (prior ~40-60 red-zone trips) with additional weight to yards-based expected TD rate (from field-position-based expected points). Track separately for 4th-down go rate inside the 5.

nfl.turnovers.label: Turnover rate and takeaway luck regression
nfl.turnovers.mechanism: Turnovers swing possession counts and field position; offensive giveaway rates are mostly QB-driven and persistent in part, while defensive takeaways (especially fumble recoveries and INTs) regress heavily.
nfl.turnovers.rationale: Forecasting should use expected turnovers from process (pressure, tipped balls, aggressive throws, ball security) rather than realized takeaways; realized takeaway differential is a notorious regressor that markets sometimes overreact to.
nfl.turnovers.measurement: Offensive giveaways per play (INT rate with QB prior, fumble rate) and defensive takeaways per play; decompose INT into turnover-worthy/pressure/deflection and fumbles into forced vs recovered; regress recovered-fumble share to 50%; use opponent-adjusted rates with long half-life. Compare realized to expected from pressure and QB aggressiveness.

nfl.fumble_luck.label: Fumble recovery luck
nfl.fumble_luck.mechanism: Roughly half of all fumbles are recovered by each side irrespective of team skill, so team and player fumbles-lost outcomes are mostly random and mean-revert.
nfl.fumble_luck.rationale: Fumbles lost are a major swing factor in single-game outcomes and in season-level takeaway/turnover counts; a team that has been lucky recovering fumbles is overrated by raw turnover differential, and a player with several fumbles lost is not as likely to repeat.
nfl.fumble_luck.measurement: Count fumbles (forced and unforced) and recoveries by team and player; compute expected lost fumbles = fumbles x ~0.5 (position-specific adjustment: QB sacks/strips, RB, special teams); luck = realized lost minus expected; apply shrinkage to zero for forward projections; use fumble rate (not lost rate) as the repeatable component.

nfl.td_luck.label: Touchdown luck and yards-to-points regression
nfl.td_luck.mechanism: Touchdowns per yard or per target for a player or team above/below the expected rate given field position and usage are largely noise, producing regression in subsequent games and in season totals.
nfl.td_luck.rationale: TD props and totals are repriced on a recent hot streak; the true expectation depends on opportunity (red-zone touches, targets inside the 10) not on realized TDs. Subtle: some players (large TE/QB sneakers) have persistently higher TD rates than yardage implies.
nfl.td_luck.measurement: TD over expected = actual TDs minus expected TDs from carry/target location (yard line, game state), using expected points/TD models (ff_opportunity expected TD fields). Shrink luck to zero (e.g. 70-85% regression) and keep a smaller persistent player/role residual estimated across seasons.

nfl.pythag_luck.label: Close-game record and Pythagorean luck
nfl.pythag_luck.mechanism: Win-loss records in one-score games and points-versus-expected wins are noisy; teams with large positive close-game luck typically regress, affecting season win totals, playoff odds and futures.
nfl.pythag_luck.rationale: Season-level markets (wins, division, playoffs) are anchored by past records; Pythagorean/EPA-based wins and one-score-game luck give a better estimate of true talent than actual wins; the subtlety is the part of one-score success that is genuinely skill (QB late game, kicker, clock).
nfl.pythag_luck.measurement: Pythagorean expectation (points^2.37 form) and EPA-based expected wins; compute record in games decided by one score or less and the deficit versus expected; regress ~80-90% of close-game luck to zero; adjust using kicker/late-game QB prior.

nfl.points_vs_expected.label: Points per drive versus drive-efficiency expectation (finishing luck)
nfl.points_vs_expected.mechanism: Points scored differ from points expected from yards and field position because of sequencing luck, FG variance, and turnover timing; this gap reverts toward zero.
nfl.points_vs_expected.rationale: A team that has scored much more than its yardage/EPA implies is expected to score less going forward; totals and team-total markets that follow recent scores can be mispriced by this sequencing noise.
nfl.points_vs_expected.measurement: For each team-game: actual points minus expected points from drive-level expected-points models (starting field position, yards gained) or EPA-based points; accumulate with recency weights; project regress to zero; track with decay so that real changes in finishing ability (kicker, QB) are slowly incorporated.

nfl.field_pos.label: Starting field position, special teams and return units
nfl.field_pos.mechanism: Average starting field position affects drive length and scoring probability (about 3 points per 10 yards of field position equivalent), determined by punting, returns, kickoffs, turnover spots and penalties.
nfl.field_pos.rationale: Special teams is a persistent but underweighted edge in game spread and totals; the 2024 kickoff rules changed touchback rates and return value, so older seasons need adjustment. Subtle: starting position also correlates with defensive quality via drive starts.
nfl.field_pos.measurement: Average starting yard line by team (own drives and opponent drives) separate from turnover-spot effect; net punt, kickoff return EPA, touchback rate by kicker; use rule-regime indicator for kickoff rules by season; shrink rate by games played.

nfl.kicker.label: Kicker accuracy by distance and effective range, kickoff touchback rate
nfl.kicker.mechanism: Kicker make probability by distance and weather determines the points value of drives that stall, FG attempt aggressiveness (range), and kickoff touchback probability.
nfl.kicker.rationale: Because roughly one-third of NFL scoring is FG/XP, kicker quality shifts team totals, kicker props and FG-versus-go decisions. Small samples demand shrinkage; wind and altitude interact strongly with long-range makes.
nfl.kicker.measurement: Logistic make probability vs distance with kicker random effect (Bayesian shrinkage with prior ~100+ attempts), stadium/altitude/wind/temp covariates; effective range = max distance with make prob >~50%; kickoff touchback rate by kicker and rule regime.

nfl.penalties.label: Team penalty rates and flag-driven drive effects
nfl.penalties.mechanism: Penalties move down-and-distance and field position; offensive holding/false starts depress EPA, defensive pass interference/holding extend drives. Team rates are partly persistent (discipline) and partly crew-driven.
nfl.penalties.rationale: Penalty-driven yardage can matter for team totals and for QB/receiver props via DPI yards; the crew effect (see officials) separates from team discipline. Registry notes it is currently not collected, so this is a hypothesis input.
nfl.penalties.measurement: Per game: accepted penalties and yards by type for offense/defense, opponent-adjusted; decompose into team-driven and referee-driven by mixed model with team and crew effects; include DPI per pass attempt.

nfl.officials_crew.label: Officiating crew penalty and call tendencies
nfl.officials_crew.mechanism: Referee crews differ in flag rates (holding, DPI, illegal contact) which affects drive length, scoring and pace; crews are announced weekly.
nfl.officials_crew.rationale: Penalty-heavy crews lengthen games and change efficiency; the effect is modest and noisy, so it needs shrinkage, but it is knowable pregame and may interact with pass-heavy offenses and DPI-heavy yardage props.
nfl.officials_crew.measurement: From nflverse officials and play_by_play, compute crew-level penalties per game, DPI per game and home-flag differential with random-effects shrinkage; control for the teams involved; map crew assignment to game (announced around Thursday of game week).

nfl.pace.label: Neutral-situation pace and plays per game
nfl.pace.mechanism: Seconds per play in neutral situations (score within a window, first three quarters) and no-huddle usage set total offensive plays, which scales every counting stat and total points.
nfl.pace.rationale: Pace is a stable team trait strongly tied to coach and QB; it is partially offset by opponent (a slow opponent reduces possessions) and by game state. Because totals and props scale linearly with plays, pace misestimation of even 3-4 plays matters; remember run-heavy teams burn clock.
nfl.pace.measurement: Neutral-situation seconds per play (win prob 20-80%, quarters 1-3) per team; combine offense and opponent defense/time-of-possession style by additive model; compute expected plays = f(pace_off, pace_def, pass rate (clock stoppage), expected script). Recency-weight, shrink toward league; flag coaching/QB changes.

nfl.drives.label: Expected drives per team and clock-killing style
nfl.drives.mechanism: The number of possessions per team is the true volume unit: more drives means more scoring chances; it depends on pace, turnover rate, punts, and clock use.
nfl.drives.rationale: Drives per game is more directly tied to scoring than plays per game and is correlated across both teams, so game totals should be modeled as drives times points per drive with opponent adjustment; lopsided scripts reduce drives for the leading team late.
nfl.drives.measurement: Drives per game (excluding kneel-downs/end-of-half) per team and for games involving it; opponent-adjusted; project via plays/drive and drive-count model with script; include expected number of kneel/end-of-half possessions.

nfl.proe.label: Pass rate over expected, neutral and script-adjusted
nfl.proe.mechanism: Pass rate over expected measures a team's tendency to pass beyond what down, distance, field position and score predict; it is mainly coach/coordinator and QB-driven and sets pass attempts, hence passing yards and target volume.
nfl.proe.rationale: PROE separates scheme from game script so that expected attempts can be forecast jointly with the spread: pass-heavy teams hold volume in neutral scripts and inflate when trailing; run-heavy teams suppress passing yardage regardless of QB quality. Coordinator changes or QB injuries shift it.
nfl.proe.measurement: Fit an expected-pass model (logistic on down, distance, yard line, score diff, time, timeouts, shotgun) on league data; PROE = mean(actual - expected) over neutral plays per team; recency weighted with coordinator/QB regime flags; then forecast attempts = expected plays x (expected pass rate given forecast score distribution + PROE).

nfl.two_minute_tempo.label: Two-minute drill and hurry-up tempo
nfl.two_minute_tempo.mechanism: End-of-half and trailing hurry-up possessions inflate pass attempts, yards and quick scoring; teams differ in two-minute efficiency and willingness to hurry.
nfl.two_minute_tempo.rationale: First-half and quarter totals and receiving props include a lot of end-of-half mass; the opposite, kneel-downs and clock killing, suppress scoring. Coaches' timeout and clock behavior makes this partly knowable.
nfl.two_minute_tempo.measurement: Per team: points, plays and pass rate in the last two minutes of each half, share of end-of-half possessions with points; opponent-adjusted; timeouts retained; QB prior in two-minute drill; combine with expected lead/trail states from the spread.

nfl.garbage_time.label: Garbage-time and blowout script mass
nfl.garbage_time.mechanism: In lopsided games the trailing team passes more, the leader runs, and backups play; this redistributes yardage and creates tail outcomes for props.
nfl.garbage_time.rationale: Garbage-time inflates stats of trailing teams' receivers/QBs and deflates the leader's passing yardage; its probability is a function of the spread and team quality and should be modelled, not ignored, for yardage ladders.
nfl.garbage_time.measurement: Estimate probability of a 14+ point lead in Q4 from spread/total and score-difference distribution; measure each team/player stat split by garbage-time vs non-garbage-time (win probability <5% or >95%); add team tendency for starters leaving; combine into expected garbage mass for each prop.

nfl.script.label: Game-script lattice: pass rate, pace and efficiency conditional on lead or trail
nfl.script.mechanism: Teams pass more and play faster when trailing and run and slow down when leading; the expected game script from the spread therefore determines volume splits between passing and rushing props.
nfl.script.rationale: Because props are priced off a spread-and-total-derived script, the model must integrate over the score-state distribution rather than use a single average; teams differ in how strongly pass rate responds to score (coaching), making the lattice team-specific.
nfl.script.measurement: From play_by_play estimate pass rate, seconds/play, rush attempts and efficiency as a function of score differential bins and time remaining; simulate or integrate with the distribution of game states implied by spread/total (e.g., Gaussian margin around spread); team-specific slope with shrinkage to league.

nfl.opening_possession.label: Opening possession and coin-toss deferral behavior
nfl.opening_possession.mechanism: Which team gets the first possession (and the second-half kickoff) changes first-quarter scoring and first TD scorer/team probabilities.
nfl.opening_possession.rationale: Coin toss is random but teams' defer rates are coach-specific; first-scoring markets are partially a function of who has the ball first. After the second-half kickoff, the deferring team opens the half, shifting second-half timing.
nfl.opening_possession.measurement: Team and coach defer rate by season (post-2008 rule), by weather and by game importance; hazard model of first score timing by possession order; unknown at market time unless the market settles after the coin toss; adjust probabilities as 50/50 prior with a team-defer-rate mixture.

nfl.opening_script.label: Opening-drive play-calling and first-drive outcomes
nfl.opening_script.mechanism: Scripted opening drives show team-specific tendencies (pass/run split, tempo, TD rate on first drive) that influence first-quarter and first-TD markets.
nfl.opening_script.rationale: The first 15 plays are pre-scripted and differ from the rest of the game; the chance of an opening-drive TD for either team determines first-TD team/time and early race-to-N markets. Small samples require shrinkage.
nfl.opening_script.measurement: For each team: share of opening drives (first drive of game and of second half) ending in TD/FG/punt/turnover, plays per drive, pass rate vs expected; first-play targets; shrink to league mean with prior ~30 drives; adjust for QB/coordinator changes.

nfl.q_scoring.label: Historical scoring by quarter and half, opponent-adjusted
nfl.q_scoring.mechanism: Scoring is unevenly distributed through the game: first-quarter scripted drives, end-of-half drives, and second-half game-state adjustments cause quarter-specific scoring rates for each team.
nfl.q_scoring.rationale: Quarter/half total and spread markets need period scoring distributions rather than scaled game totals; end-of-half possessions and halftime adjustments make second half scoring different, and team styles (slow starters, strong two-minute offense) are persistent in part.
nfl.q_scoring.measurement: Per team: points and plays by quarter/half, opponent-adjusted; compute the team's share of expected game points scored in each period; shrink to league period shares (Q1 lower, Q2 and Q4 higher); combine team and opponent scoring shares with the game total from market.

nfl.qb.label: Starting QB status and QB-specific regime

nfl.team_total_split.rationale: Team total and combined markets must be consistent with the game market; the split depends on spread and total only if the market is efficient; deviations signal mispricing; allowing for scoring styles (high-variance team) matters.
nfl.team_total_split.measurement: Compute implied team means from the closing spread and total (mu_A = (T - s)/2 etc.), adjust for team-specific scoring variance and key-number structure; compare team total quotes to the implied pair to detect inconsistent pricing.

nfl.safety_risk.label: Safety and special-play event risk

nfl.safety_risk.rationale: Rare-event props such as safety, defensive/special-teams TDs and 2-point conversions need base rates conditioned on pass rush, OL quality, field position and offensive style; the per-game base rate is low so shrinkage and pooling are essential.

nfl.leader_order_statistic.mechanism: Leader markets resolve to the maximum across many players with correlated outcomes; the probability that a given player leads depends on the top-end distribution of competitors, not just his own mean.
nfl.leader_order_statistic.rationale: The favorite's probability is bounded by variance of many near contenders; per-game weekly leaders (e.g. most receiving yards) are far more random than season leaders; pricing should use simulation of the whole field with correlations.

nfl.fantasy_points_model.label: Fantasy-points translation (PPR component model)

nfl.award_stats.label: Award-candidate production and voting narrative

nfl.award_voting_mechanics.label: Award voter pool, timing and tie rules

nfl.draft_board.label: Draft order, prospect rankings and team needs

nfl.cap_and_contract.label: Cap space, contract status and transaction signals

nfl.novelty_prop_priors.label: Novelty and event base rates (coin toss, anthem, halftime, mentions)

nfl.offfield_base_rate.label: Reference-class base rates for NFL off-field events

nfl.player_xtd.label: Player expected touchdowns (xTD) from play-level opportunity
nfl.player_xtd.mechanism: Each rushing attempt and target carries a modelled TD probability that depends on yard line, down and distance, and play type; summing gives an opportunity-based TD expectation independent of luck.
nfl.player_xtd.rationale: Season TD counts and TD rates are dominated by finishing luck (a back with 6 carries inside the 5 can score 0-6). xTD collapses to the opportunity and removes the single-season noise that makes nfl.td_rates misleading.
nfl.player_xtd.measurement: For each rush attempt or target in the player's last 17 team games (half-life 6 games), assign P(TD | yardline_100, down, ydstogo, play_type, is_target) from a league-wide model fit on 2006+ pbp; sum by player; divide by team xTD to get a share. Shrink share to positional prior with k=4 team games' worth of goal-line touches. As-of: through the previous game; recompute after inactives.

nfl.goal_line_personnel.label: Goal-line package and personnel tree (inside the 5)
nfl.goal_line_personnel.mechanism: In goal-to-go snaps inside about the 5-yard line, teams switch to heavy sets (extra TE/OL, FB) and select specific ball carriers and a QB-sneak option, so the TD-eligible set differs from the field-wide rotation.
nfl.goal_line_personnel.rationale: A back who plays 70% of snaps may have zero goal-line role; a 250-pound change-of-pace back may play 5% of snaps and take 60% of inside-the-3 carries. The share of snaps and the share of goal-line carries are different quantities.

nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.label: 4th-and-goal and goal-to-go go-for-it policy
nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.mechanism: On 4th-and-goal from inside the 2-3 yards, coaches either kick a FG or go for the TD, changing the number of TDs and the target and carry mix on those snaps.
nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.rationale: TD pool is what matters, not points; two teams with equal implied totals can differ by half a TD per game because of this choice. It also drives who receives the final-yard touches.
nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.measurement: Go-for-it rate on 4th-and-goal with ydstogo <= 3 over the last 2 seasons, opponent and win-probability adjusted: logistic regression on wp, ydstogo, score_differential, time; coach-level random effect with k=12 attempts shrinkage; as-of last game of the prior week; flagged on coach change.

nfl.team_first_td_attribution.label: Team first-TD scorer attribution history
nfl.team_first_td_attribution.mechanism: The scorer of a team's first TD is drawn from a distribution that differs from the full-game distribution because the first score arises in scripted and early-down contexts.
nfl.team_first_td_attribution.rationale: Scorer shares in first TDs are rated off about 17 events per team-season, so they need strong shrinkage to the full-game xTD share; naive 'first TD hit rate' is nearly pure noise.
nfl.team_first_td_attribution.measurement: For each team-game, record the scorer of the team's first TD and the yard line; compute recency-weighted shares (half-life 20 team games, includes prior-season games at 0.5 weight) and shrink to the player's full-game xTD share with k=10 team first-TD events; output: scorer share and expected yardline.

nfl.dst_td_hazard.label: Defensive and special-teams TD hazard per team-game
nfl.dst_td_hazard.mechanism: Pick-sixes, fumble returns, punt and kick return TDs happen at low frequency and are partly attributable to scheme and returner skill but largely random.
nfl.dst_td_hazard.rationale: These events end the 'first TD' contest for every offensive player and count in the team first-TD and D/ST TD markets; they are about 1 in 8-10 team games.
nfl.dst_td_hazard.measurement: Per team-game rate = 0.5*(own takeaway-return TD rate regressed to league mean with k=40 team games + opponent giveaway rate) + returner threat (kick and punt return TD per return, k=60 returns) + opponent special teams allowed rate. Poisson mean; as-of previous game.

nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.label: Active-but-zero-snap and protected-void probability
nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.mechanism: A player can be active and take no snap (RB3, TE3, gadget WR), which voids the contract, and protected contracts void on first-half-only exposure.
nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.rationale: The contract is conditional on a snap; ignoring this overstates a low-usage player's effective price and misses the void probability that determines how much capital is truly at risk.
nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.measurement: P(no snap | active) = fraction of last 12 active games with zero offensive snaps, shrunk with a beta prior by depth-chart slot (k=6); P(first-half-only) = fraction of active games with snaps in 1H and none in 2H, plus a Friday-designation uplift from past data; as-of 90-minute inactive list.

nfl.multi_td_dispersion.label: Within-player multi-TD dispersion factor
nfl.multi_td_dispersion.mechanism: A player's TDs share a latent intensity (team total and goal-line role), so P(2+) exceeds the Poisson implied by P(1+).
nfl.multi_td_dispersion.rationale: 2+ TD contracts and 'multiple touchdowns' markets are priced off the same marginal intensity; dispersion decides the tail ratio P(2+)/P(1+).
nfl.multi_td_dispersion.measurement: Fit a negative-binomial dispersion r by position group (RB goal-line, WR1, TE, QB rush) on the last 5 seasons of player-games with at least 4 expected TD-opportunity touches; report r and P(2+|P(1+)) lookup table; as-of start of week.

nfl.model_team_td_mean.label: Market-free team touchdown mean (drives times TD-per-drive, with FG-vs-TD split)
nfl.model_team_td_mean.mechanism: A team's expected touchdowns are expected drives times the per-drive probability of ending in a touchdown rather than a field goal or no score, estimated from opponent-adjusted offence and defence and red-zone conversion, with no spread, total or price as a feature.
nfl.model_team_td_mean.rationale: Every scorer market is a share of the team's touchdown pool. A points-based implied team total is market-derived and is not touchdown-specific (24 points can be 3 TD + FG or 2 TD + 3 FG). A model-derived TD mean keeps wind, availability and matchup visible and gives P(team scores at least one TD), the quantity the team-own first-TD contract depends on.
nfl.model_team_td_mean.measurement: lambda_TD(team i vs j) = E[drives_i] x P(TD | drive). E[drives] from both teams' neutral seconds per play and expected plays (2015+ pbp, shrink 50/50 to league at 8 games). P(TD|drive) = logistic ridge on own opponent-adjusted offensive EPA per play (half-life 8 games, prior-season weight 0.3 fading to 0 by week 10), opponent defensive EPA per play, red-zone trips per drive and red-zone TD rate (shrunk k=30 trips), 4th-and-goal go-for-it rate (k=12), wind>15 mph and dome flags, starting-QB indicator. Output mean, variance (overdispersion from tercile residuals) and P(N>=1)=1-exp(-lambda_TD) with a negative-binomial correction. As-of: after the previous game, refreshed at the final injury report. Spreads, totals and prices excluded; used only afterwards as a benchmark.

nfl.leg_dependence_by_margin_regime.label: Leg-pair dependence conditioned on margin and total regime
nfl.leg_dependence_by_margin_regime.mechanism: Cross-leg dependence between pairs such as favourite cover and QB yards, or total over and rusher yards, changes sign by game regime (competitive, favourite blowout, shootout).
nfl.leg_dependence_by_margin_regime.rationale: A single correlation coefficient averages a positive correlation in shootouts with a negative one in blowouts, understating joint probabilities for some leg sets and overstating for others.
nfl.leg_dependence_by_margin_regime.measurement: For each leg-type pair (about 30 types), estimate the Kendall tau or tetrachoric correlation of the two leg indicators within bins of pregame spread (|s|<3, 3-7, >7) and total terciles, using 2015+ player-games; shrink bin estimates toward the pooled estimate with k=150 games; require 400+ games per cell; report standard errors; as-of end of previous week.
free_sources: nflverse pbp, player_stats, schedules (spread and total fields)

nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.label: Team-to-player accounting constraints for same-game legs
nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.mechanism: Individual player outputs must sum to team outputs, so player legs on one team compete for a fixed pool, and incompatible leg sets have zero joint probability.
nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.rationale: Gaussian correlations allow two teammates to both hit first-TD legs or both clear very large yardage lines; the identity-based approach prevents impossible combinations and captures negative dependence among teammates.
nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.measurement: Compute, from historical player-games, the distribution of the share of team yards and TDs captured by the top-k players; define a Dirichlet-multinomial allocation for each team-game with concentration from the prior 17 games (shrink k=20); enforce sum(player) = team and floor for unlisted players. Output joint distribution over pairs of player legs on one team; as-of previous game.

nfl.common_availability_shock.label: Shared availability shock across legs (QB, WR1, OL, kicker)
nfl.common_availability_shock.mechanism: One lineup event (QB scratch, kicker injury, star WR late scratch) moves several legs of the same combo simultaneously.
nfl.common_availability_shock.rationale: Legs priced early assume a baseline lineup; a late change lowers the QB yards leg, total and favourite-cover jointly, so the joint probability is a mixture over lineup states rather than a product.
nfl.common_availability_shock.measurement: Define lineup states (QB1/QB2, WR1 in/out, starting kicker, RT in/out) with probabilities from injury designation base rates (shrink to position-level, k=10 games); condition each leg on state using prior-season splits with k=3 games shrinkage; joint = sum over states of P(state) x product of conditional legs adjusted by in-state dependence. As-of per injury report vintage.

nfl.leg_void_push_matrix.label: Per-leg void, push and overtime state matrix
nfl.leg_void_push_matrix.mechanism: Each leg type has deterministic rules for pushes, postponement, no-snap voids and overtime that define the joint event and its payout.
nfl.leg_void_push_matrix.rationale: Combo payoff differs between a pushed leg being dropped or the combo lost; near 3 and 7 on integer spreads the push mass is 6-9% of games and cannot be ignored.
nfl.leg_void_push_matrix.measurement: Table with columns: leg_series, includes_OT (yes/no/unknown), push_possible (integer line), void_rule, fair_price_rule, source text hash and date; join to the combo's rules text; for each combo, compute P(joint | rule variant) for each variant of the unknown combo wording and carry the spread as model uncertainty. As-of rules text version captured at order time.
free_sources: Kalshi API rules_primary and rules_secondary (free, own_capture for versions)

nfl.model_team_points_mean.label: Market-free team expected points and margin (drive-model mean and SD per team)
nfl.model_team_points_mean.mechanism: Each team's expected points are expected drives times points per drive, built from opponent-adjusted offence and defence efficiency, tempo, kicker and quarterback status and weather, with no betting line, price or implied total used as a feature.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.rationale: Market-derived team means (spread and total splits) are benchmarks that already contain the market's injury, weather and sharp information; feeding them into a model of the same game makes the model unable to show any independent information and hides which fundamental channels are missing. A market-free mean keeps the availability, weather, matchup and coaching channels explicit and lets the line be used only as an evaluation benchmark.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.measurement: For team i vs opponent j, expected points = E[drives_i] x E[points per drive_i]. E[drives] = 3600 / (mean seconds per drive implied by both teams' neutral-situation seconds per play and expected plays per drive), 2015+ regular-season pbp, ridge-shrunk 50/50 toward league mean at 8 games. Points per drive from a ridge regression on own opponent-adjusted offensive EPA per play (exponential half-life 8 games, prior-season carryover weight 0.3 decaying to 0 by week 10), opponent defensive EPA per play, red-zone TD rate (shrunk k=30 trips), kicker FG-range rating, starting-QB indicator, wind above 15 mph and dome flags, home indicator. Output team mean, SD (from residuals by tercile) and the margin and total means as differences and sums. As-of timestamp: after the previous game and re-run at the latest injury report. Betting lines are excluded from the feature set and used only for after-the-fact benchmarking.
free_sources: nflverse pbp and schedules (EPA, drives, seconds per play, wind, roof)
nflverse injuries and depth charts (QB status)

nfl.model_margin_lattice.label: Model-based regulation margin lattice with mass at zero (key-number corrected, end-of-game behaviour included)
nfl.model_margin_lattice.mechanism: Probability that the regulation margin equals k, especially k=0, from a drive-outcome simulation or lattice centred on the market-free team means, corrected for the excess mass that 3-point and 7-point scoring and late tie-forcing behaviour put on small margins.
nfl.model_margin_lattice.rationale: Tie, overtime and integer-spread markets are priced on atoms at specific margins, which a smooth normal density misses; a lattice centred on betting-line residuals would import the market's own view of the game. Centring on the model mean margin and total from the market-free team means keeps the input market-free and lets the line serve as a benchmark only.
nfl.model_margin_lattice.measurement: Simulate 20,000 games per matchup from per-drive outcome multinomials (TD with 94 percent extra-point conversion, FG, safety, no score) calibrated so team means equal the market-free model team means, then fit an isotonic correction of simulated P(margin=k) to empirical regulation-margin frequencies (all regular-season games since 2002, about 5,500, binned by model |mean margin| in 0-3, 3-6, 6-10, 10+ points and model total terciles) with Beta(a=2, b=30) shrinkage in each bin for k=0 and Dirichlet smoothing for key numbers 3, 6, 7, 10, 14. Add an end-of-game term for tied games where the team with the ball inside two minutes can run the clock. Output P(margin=k) for k from -30 to 30. As-of: latest model means at kickoff minus 90 minutes; no spread, total or price enters.
free_sources: nflverse schedules/results (final regulation scores by quarter)

nfl.drive_clock_allocation.label: Drive-start allocation across periods (clock-resolved)
nfl.drive_clock_allocation.mechanism: The number of drives that begin in each quarter, and where the quarter ends relative to drive boundaries, for both teams.
nfl.drive_clock_allocation.rationale: Quarter totals depend on counts of starts and finishes in a 15-minute window; a game-level drives estimate ignores kickoff order, tempo by period, and clock burn.
nfl.drive_clock_allocation.measurement: From pbp: for each team-game, count drives starting in Q1..Q4 and seconds per drive by period; use 20-game recency weights (half-life 8) and opponent-adjust by regressing on opponent pace; combine with kickoff order to produce expected starts for each quarter and the probability of a second drive in Q1. Shrink to league mean with k=10 games.

nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.label: Opponent-adjusted per-drive TD/FG rates by period
nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.mechanism: Per-drive probability of TD, FG and no score separately for Q1, Q2 (including two-minute drives), Q3 and Q4 by team and opponent.
nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.rationale: Team quality is measured on all plays; period rates differ because scripted openers and hurry-up drills have different efficiency, and Q4 depends on game state; averaging understates the spread of per-quarter rates.
nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.measurement: Multinomial (TD, FG, no score) logistic with team offence and opponent defence random effects per period, fitted on 3 seasons with exponential decay (half-life 12 team games); shrink period effects to the team's all-period rate with k=30 drives; as-of previous game; exclude garbage-time Q4 drives (win probability <5% or >95%) from the training sample and treat them separately.

nfl.period_zero_tie_mass.label: Zero-score and tied-period mass by quarter
nfl.period_zero_tie_mass.mechanism: Empirical and model probabilities of 0-0 in a quarter, an equal non-zero score, and BTTS by quarter.
nfl.period_zero_tie_mass.rationale: Tie strike, 'both teams score' and over 7.5 are determined by the atoms of the joint distribution, which a Gaussian or Poisson-total approximation badly misstates.
nfl.period_zero_tie_mass.measurement: From 2010+ team-quarters: frequencies of each (home, away) score pair by quarter; smooth with a bivariate model whose marginal means come from the drive-allocation and per-drive rates; calibrate atom masses at 0, 3, 7 with isotonic regression; report P(0-0), P(tie), P(BTTS) by quarter and total scoring tercile; as-of start of season with rolling refresh.
free_sources: nflverse pbp / schedules with period scores

nfl.halftime_state_conditional_scoring.label: Second-half scoring conditional on halftime margin
nfl.halftime_state_conditional_scoring.mechanism: Second-half scoring and the split Q3/Q4 depend on halftime margin and the team's script response.
nfl.halftime_state_conditional_scoring.rationale: 3Q and 4Q totals/spreads are mixtures; the same team plays differently when leading by 14 vs trailing by 3, and pregame it must be mixed over halftime states.
nfl.halftime_state_conditional_scoring.measurement: Condition historical Q3 and Q4 team points on halftime margin bins (<=-10, -9..-4, -3..+3, +4..+9, >=+10) and on pregame spread; use kernel-weighted estimates (bandwidth 3 points of margin) shrunk to team-level second-half scoring with k=15 games; mixture weights from the pregame margin distribution; as-of start of week.

nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.label: Cross-quarter dependence of team scoring
nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.mechanism: The correlation between a team scoring in quarter j and in quarter k, accounting for pace, quality and clock burn.
nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.rationale: Every-quarter BTTS and 1H/2H combos require the joint of period events, which differs from the product of marginals.
nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.measurement: Compute tetrachoric correlations of team-scored-in-quarter indicators across quarter pairs from 2015+ team-games, split by team offensive EPA tercile; compare to the independence benchmark; shrink pairwise estimates toward the pooled with k=300 games; as-of season-to-date.

nfl.kickoff_rule_regime.label: Kickoff and touchback rule regime and return rates
nfl.kickoff_rule_regime.mechanism: League kickoff rules (dynamic kickoff, touchback spot, setup zone) set the starting field position for Q1 and Q3 drives and for post-score drives.
nfl.kickoff_rule_regime.rationale: Rule changes since 2024 moved touchback placement and return rates, shifting early field position and short-field scoring; models fit to older seasons carry stale starting-position values.
nfl.kickoff_rule_regime.measurement: Per-season distribution of starting yard line after kickoffs, touchback rate, return rate and return TD rate; effective expected starting field position by team returner (k=20 returns shrinkage); flag season of rule change and refit; as-of week.
free_sources: NFL rulebook and competition committee announcements

nfl.drive_outcome_by_index.label: Per-drive outcome probabilities by drive index and starting field position
nfl.drive_outcome_by_index.mechanism: Multinomial outcome of drive 1, 2 and 3 for each team, conditional on starting yard line and opponent.
nfl.drive_outcome_by_index.rationale: The first drive is scripted and starts from a kickoff; season-average drive efficiency misses the hazard that matters for first-score contracts.
nfl.drive_outcome_by_index.measurement: Fit multinomial logit (TD, FG, punt, turnover, other) on the first four team drives of each game 2015+ with covariates: team offence random effect, opponent defence random effect, starting yardline_100; recency half-life 15 games; shrink team early-drive effect toward its all-drive effect with k=25 early drives; as-of previous game.
free_sources: nflverse pbp (drive-level via fixed_drive and drive result)

nfl.drive_duration_by_outcome.label: Drive duration distribution by outcome and team style
nfl.drive_duration_by_outcome.mechanism: Seconds of game clock consumed by TD drives, FG drives, punts and turnovers for each team and opponent.
nfl.drive_duration_by_outcome.rationale: The time of the first TD (and bucket probabilities) is a convolution of these durations, so mean pace is insufficient; the right tail matters for late buckets.
nfl.drive_duration_by_outcome.measurement: From pbp: drive_time_of_possession by outcome for each team over the last 20 games (half-life 10); opponent adjustment by regression on the opponent's allowed durations; fit a lognormal for each outcome class with team-level scale shrunk to league with k=15 drives; as-of previous game; clock-converted to elapsed game clock including quarter-end stops.

nfl.scoring_event_point_values.label: Scoring package distribution (TD value, extra points, two-point, safety)
nfl.scoring_event_point_values.mechanism: Points per TD depend on the extra-point success rate and two-point attempt policy; FG is 3; safeties 2.
nfl.scoring_event_point_values.rationale: Race-to-N lattices depend on the exact increment distribution; treating a TD as 7 misses 6-point and 8-point cases that change which team crosses N first.
nfl.scoring_event_point_values.measurement: Per team: P(XP made | kicker, distance) with k=50 attempts shrinkage; two-point attempt rate by coach and win probability state with k=15; safety rate per game; compute P(TD value in {6,7,8}); as-of start of week.

nfl.early_nonoffensive_score_hazard.label: Early-game non-offensive scoring hazard (pick-six, return TD, safety)
nfl.early_nonoffensive_score_hazard.mechanism: Probability of a defensive, return or safety score in the first half of the opening quarter or before the first offensive TD.
nfl.early_nonoffensive_score_hazard.rationale: Such scores pre-empt the race and occur on a different hazard from offensive drives; ignoring them biases first-team probabilities toward the stronger offence.
nfl.early_nonoffensive_score_hazard.measurement: Hazard per team-game of non-offensive TD (own takeaway returns + returner threat + opponent giveaways) and safety, estimated over 3 seasons with k=40 team-games shrinkage; allocate within the first 15 game minutes using the empirical share of such events by quarter (about one quarter of events); as-of previous game.

nfl.opening_kick_field_position.label: Opening kickoff field position distribution by returner and rule regime
nfl.opening_kick_field_position.mechanism: Starting yard line after the opening kickoff (touchback spot, return average, return TD risk).
nfl.opening_kick_field_position.rationale: Field position at drive 1 changes TD probability for the first drive; rule changes alter the touchback spot and return frequency season to season.
nfl.opening_kick_field_position.measurement: Per team's returner and kicker: P(touchback), mean starting yardline_100 after kick, return TD per kickoff, shrunk to league by season with k=20 kicks; flag the season-specific rule; as-of week.

nfl.late_tie_game_management.label: Late-game tie-state management policy
nfl.late_tie_game_management.mechanism: In the last two minutes with the score level, trailing by 3 or leading by 3, coaches choose between kneeling, kicking a game-winning FG, or pushing; these decisions concentrate regulation margin mass at 0.
nfl.late_tie_game_management.rationale: The margin distribution at zero is partly behavioural: a team tied with the ball inside two minutes may run the clock to guarantee overtime, and a team trailing by 3 kicks a tying FG. A smooth score model misses this.
nfl.late_tie_game_management.measurement: From pbp: for each coach and season, rate of kneel-downs, FG attempts and go-for-it when score diff in {-3..0} and game_seconds_remaining<=120; shrink to league with k=10 occasions; compute P(tie at final | state) by state and apply to the simulated margin distribution; as-of previous week.

nfl.ot_ending_hazard.label: P(game ends level | overtime) under current OT rules
nfl.ot_ending_hazard.mechanism: Probability that the overtime period fails to produce a decisive score, given each team's possession counts, scoring rates and 4th-down choices under the OT rule set.
nfl.ot_ending_hazard.rationale: Overtime ending level is a very small but rule-dependent event; the tie market is the product of two small probabilities and the OT-rule change makes historical frequencies stale.
nfl.ot_ending_hazard.measurement: Simulate OT as a drive process with period length 10 min (regular season), possession rule per season, team TD/FG rates per drive (from nfl.drive-level data, shrunk), and 4th-down aggression; calibrate to realized OT outcomes since 2012 (about 100+ regular-season OT games); report P(level | OT) with credible interval; as-of start of season and refreshed weekly.
free_sources: nflverse schedules and pbp (overtime flag, result)

nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.label: End-zone exposure plays per team-game
nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.mechanism: Count of offensive plays run with the ball inside the team's own 5-yard line and punts from within the own end zone or 5, which are the sites of most safeties.
nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.rationale: Safeties scale with exposure; a team that starts drives deep and has a poor punt unit has several times more exposed plays than another.
nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.measurement: From pbp: per team-game count of offensive plays with yardline_100>=95 plus punts with yardline_100>=90, with a per-play safety probability by play type (sack, run, pass, punt) from 2010+ league data, team factor shrunk with k=30 exposed plays; recency half-life 20 games; expected safeties = sum count x probability; as-of previous game.

nfl.rush_yardage_tail.label: Per-carry yardage tail (explosive-run probability) by rusher
nfl.rush_yardage_tail.mechanism: Mixture distribution of rushing yards per carry for the named player: P(10+), P(20+), P(40+) per carry after opponent adjustment.
nfl.rush_yardage_tail.rationale: The maximum over N carries is governed by tail probabilities, not average yards per carry; two backs with equal averages have different longest-rush distributions.
nfl.rush_yardage_tail.measurement: For rushers (RB and QB separately) fit a discrete tail: P(yards>=k per carry) for k in {7, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40} on 3 seasons of carries, half-life 25 carries; shrink to positional prior with k=60 carries; adjust by opponent run-defence tail rate (stuff and explosive-allowed) with k=100 carries; as-of previous game.
free_sources: Next Gen Stats rushing (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for public access)

nfl.carry_count_forecast.label: Named-player carry count distribution by script
nfl.carry_count_forecast.mechanism: Forecast distribution of the player's number of carries given team spread, game script, role and injury designation.
nfl.carry_count_forecast.rationale: N, the number of draws for the maximum, is overdispersed; a leading team gives the back 25 carries, a trailing team 10; zero for no-play voids.
nfl.carry_count_forecast.measurement: Negative binomial for carries with mean from role share (snap-weighted, half-life 6 games) times team rush attempts (spread-conditioned: mean attempts by closing spread bucket), dispersion by role; shrink share to depth-chart prior with k=3 games; include probability of 0 carries from nfl.injuries_pit; as-of inactive list.

nfl.lineup_adjusted_team_rating.label: Lineup-adjusted team rating (position-weighted value over replacement)
nfl.lineup_adjusted_team_rating.mechanism: Team margin rating is rebuilt each week as a sum of position-weighted player values over replacement for the players expected to play, rather than a team average.
nfl.lineup_adjusted_team_rating.rationale: Team EPA averages blend games with and without key starters; the effective rating for a given Sunday depends on who is active, which is known (partially) at known timestamps. Position weights differ greatly: QB, OT, EDGE, CB1 matter more per player than interior positions.
nfl.lineup_adjusted_team_rating.measurement: Per position slot s (QB, LT, RT, C, G, TE, WR1-3, RB, EDGE1-2, DT, LB, CB1-2, S), estimate weight w_s as the points-per-game coefficient from a ridge regression of team game margin residuals (actual margin minus the rating_state_space expectation, not a betting line) on player-availability indicators (2015+, ridge lambda chosen by cross-validation); value of a starter = w_s x (his performance index - replacement index), replacement index from the backup's snaps; sum over active starters; update at each injury report vintage and at the inactive list; as-of timestamp.
free_sources: nflverse rosters, injuries, depth charts, snap_counts

nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.label: Conditional margin variance model
nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.mechanism: Standard deviation and shape of the final margin as a function of expected total, spread magnitude, pace, weather and QB state.
nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.rationale: The fixed SD of 13 points misprices tails: a low-total, windy game has a narrower margin distribution than a shootout; cover probability at +/- 10 differs by regime for the same mean.
nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.measurement: Fit quantile regression (or location-scale model with t-distributed errors) of final margin on the model mean margin and model total from nfl.model_team_points_mean (not betting lines), wind, dome, backup-QB flag and divisional flag, with data 2010+ (about 4,500 games); report conditional SD and 5/95% tail multipliers; refit annually; as-of pregame values. Betting lines are excluded from the feature set and used only to benchmark the fitted SD after the fact.

nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.label: Blowout tail model for margins above 21 points
nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.mechanism: Extreme-margin probability as a function of mismatch, QB state, turnover snowballing and weather.
nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.rationale: Deep rungs (20+) and season-maximum blowout contracts are priced on the tail and a normal fit materially understates them; the distribution of margins above 28 across 2000+ is thick.
nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.measurement: Fit generalized Pareto (threshold 21) to |margin| for 2000+ games with covariates: |model expected margin| bucket from nfl.model_team_points_mean, backup QB, model total; estimate shape xi with bootstrap CI; expected number of games above k in a season = sum over games of P(|M|>k); for season max compute 1 - prod(1 - p_g); as-of start of week.

nfl.slate_total_extremes.label: Slate-level highest-total and largest-margin order statistics
nfl.slate_total_extremes.mechanism: Joint distribution of the week's game totals and margins, for maxima and tie-splitting.
nfl.slate_total_extremes.rationale: The highest-scoring game market and weekly max margin are maxima over 13-16 games with heterogeneous means; ties split the payout so exact integer ties matter.
nfl.slate_total_extremes.measurement: For each slate game g draw total from the game-total distribution (mean from nfl.pace/off_epa model, SD from nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd analog for totals), include shared weather correlation (rho from nfl.corr), simulate 20,000 slates; report P(game g has highest total) and expected payout under $1/N split; as-of kickoff vintages for each game.

nfl.rating_state_space.label: Team-strength state-space updating rule (preseason prior, process noise, opponent adjustment)
nfl.rating_state_space.mechanism: Team ratings are latent states updated weekly with an offseason regression to the mean and weekly process noise, with opponent adjustment simultaneously solved.
nfl.rating_state_space.rationale: Different updating speeds produce different mid-season ratings; slow updating misses real changes, fast updating chases noise; the choice is rarely defined in the catalog.
nfl.rating_state_space.measurement: Kalman filter on team offence and defence EPA/play ratings: state_t+1 = 0.6*state_t + 0.4*preseason_prior at season boundary (coefficient estimated by prior-year to next-year correlation 2005+), weekly process variance sigma_p^2 estimated by marginal likelihood, observation = opponent-adjusted game EPA with garbage-time weights; report posterior mean and variance per team as-of previous week.

nfl.total_plays_state_model.label: State-conditional total plays model (mutual tempo with lead effects)
nfl.total_plays_state_model.mechanism: Total plays are a function of both teams' seconds per play, run rates, expected lead state and clock stoppages rather than the average of two neutral paces.
nfl.total_plays_state_model.rationale: Neutral pace is measured when the score is close; actual plays depend on how the game goes, and a favourite protecting a lead cuts plays substantially; the combination of two paces is not additive.
nfl.total_plays_state_model.measurement: Regress total plays per game on each team's neutral seconds per play, PROE, own and opponent run rate, expected absolute margin (from model, not market), pass-completion rate and penalty rate, with team and opponent random effects; use 2015+ games; shrink coefficients; output expected plays and SD; as-of previous week.

nfl.total_distribution_tail.label: Both-tail model of game total points
nfl.total_distribution_tail.mechanism: Tail probabilities of the combined score beyond about 1.8 SD in each direction conditional on expected total and environment.
nfl.total_distribution_tail.rationale: TOTALPRECISE ladders extend to 98.5 and TOTAL to 24.5; these rungs are priced on tails, which a normal approximation gets wrong because totals are right-skewed with heavy upper tail from blowout cascades and short-field TDs. The expected total it conditions on is the market-free model total, so the tail does not inherit the line.
nfl.total_distribution_tail.measurement: Fit a skewed distribution (shifted lognormal or discrete mixture of negative-binomial team scores) to 2000+ game totals conditioned on the model expected total (sum of the market-free team means from nfl.model_team_points_mean, not a betting total) in terciles and weather regime; add empirical atoms at key totals (37, 41, 43, 44, 47, 51) as residuals of a smoothed fit with Dirichlet smoothing; estimate P(total >= 70), P(<=24) with bootstrap CI (about 5,000 games); validate calibration by decile of model expected total; as-of start of season and each week.

nfl.weather_total_response.label: Weather dose-response function for totals (wind, cold, precipitation, roof)
nfl.weather_total_response.mechanism: Estimated effect on expected total points of wind speed, temperature and precipitation categories with roof interactions.
nfl.weather_total_response.rationale: Weather effects are strongly nonlinear: below 10 mph wind is negligible, above 15-20 mph reduces totals by several points; forecast error needs to be handled at the pregame time. Historical fits use observed (not forecast) conditions until a season of forecast capture exists.
nfl.weather_total_response.measurement: Hierarchical regression of total points residual (game total minus team-baseline expectation from EPA model) on wind (piecewise linear with knots 10, 15, 20 mph), temperature (knots 32, 50), precipitation flag, dome flag; 2010+ games; shrink with k=100 games per bin; use forecast vintages 24 and 3 hours pregame and propagate forecast error as measurement noise; as-of pregame forecast.
free_sources: nflverse schedules (wind, temp as measured at game)

nfl.ot_total_increment.label: Overtime points increment and probability by rule era
nfl.ot_total_increment.mechanism: Points scored in overtime and the probability of reaching overtime, by season rule set.
nfl.ot_total_increment.rationale: If overtime counts for the contract, the total shifts by the OT points; under the rule changes of 2012-2025 OT length and possession rules changed, so frequency and points differ by era.
nfl.ot_total_increment.measurement: P(OT) by closing spread bucket and total bucket from 2012+ (about 4,000 games), expected OT points = mean points scored in OT by rule era (10-minute regular-season period), distribution of OT points (0, 3, 6, 7, 10); report contribution to total; flag current-season rule; as-of start of season.

nfl.event_calendar_hazard.label: Calendar-structured hazard curve by event type
nfl.event_calendar_hazard.mechanism: Time-varying hazard of each event type (coach exit, retirement, signing, trade, cut) across the league calendar.
nfl.event_calendar_hazard.rationale: Contracts with fixed dates (before Mar 1, 2027) integrate the hazard over uneven time; ignoring the spikes (Black Monday, cut-down, deadline) misallocates probability across the window.
nfl.event_calendar_hazard.measurement: From the transaction wire and coach history 2000-2025, count events per calendar week by type; estimate piecewise-constant weekly hazard with Gamma-Poisson shrinkage (prior shape 2, rate 4 pseudo-team-years); condition on state (team win % bin, contract year remaining); compute P(event in [now, deadline]) = 1 - exp(-sum of hazard x exposure); as-of date.

nfl.insider_report_conversion.label: Insider report-to-official-announcement conversion and lag
nfl.insider_report_conversion.mechanism: Probability and delay with which a report by a given insider and wording is followed by the official act.
nfl.insider_report_conversion.rationale: Settlement requires the official act; report credibility and lag determine whether the event resolves before the market closes.
nfl.insider_report_conversion.measurement: Build a table of reports (reporter, timestamp, wording class: 'agreed', 'expected', 'discussing') for 2018-2025, link to the official action; estimate conversion rate and median lag by reporter tier and wording with beta prior (alpha=2, beta=2) shrinkage; as-of report timestamp; output P(official within horizon).
free_sources: X/Twitter and NFL Network archives (own_capture needed)
Pro Football Reference transactions for official dates

nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.label: Initial 53-man roster inclusion model
nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.mechanism: Probability that a player is on the initial 53-man active roster given draft round, guarantees, preseason usage, position depth and injury status.
nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.rationale: Inclusion is a constrained selection with an explicit IR/PUP exclusion; stars on IR resolve NO, while fringe players depend on dead-cap cost and roster composition.
nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.measurement: Logistic regression on 2010-2025 cut-down histories: draft round, years of service, fully-secured (non-releasable) salary share, dead-cap cost of release, preseason snaps share, position group count vs slot count, injury designation at cut-down (IR/PUP/NFI flags as hard exclusion), special-teams snaps; shrink by team random effect (k=5 players per team); as-of cut-down eve.

nfl.coach_exit_hazard.label: Head-coach exit hazard (firing, resignation, pre-announced departure)
nfl.coach_exit_hazard.mechanism: Hazard of a head coach leaving or announcing departure as a function of record vs expectation, contract status, owner history and calendar.
nfl.coach_exit_hazard.rationale: The contract counts announced exits, so resignations, retirements and mutual parting count; the hazard rises sharply after the season and after specific loss patterns.
nfl.coach_exit_hazard.measurement: Cox or discrete-time logistic hazard with covariates: win% minus preseason expectation (using non-market expectation from ratings), consecutive losses, playoff outcome, years remaining on contract (0-1 vs more), tenure, owner's historical turnover, GM tenure, prior-season record; train on 2000-2025 coach-seasons (about 800); report weekly hazard in-season and post-season; as-of date.

nfl.vote_outcome_model.label: Vote-share model for awards and the Top 100 list
nfl.vote_outcome_model.mechanism: Winner or rank probability from candidate quality, narrative, previous votes, timing and electorate composition.
nfl.vote_outcome_model.rationale: Awards and ranks are decided by a small electorate with identifiable biases (position, team success, prior awards); the leader's share is concentrated.
nfl.vote_outcome_model.measurement: Multinomial logit of historical winner on candidate features (team win%, individual statistical rank, prior award wins, position, narrative flags) for each award 2000-2025 with k=3 pseudo-observations shrinkage; for T100, ordered logit on previous rank, change in production, position group and age; compute P(candidate=winner) and P(rank=#r); as-of announcement date. Aggregation layer: for division or conference specials (KXNFLMVPSPECIALS, KXNFLOPOYSPECIALS, DPOY specials) P(group) = sum over candidates of P(win) by the team of record at announcement time, with the sampled 1/N co-winner payout rule; for Executive of the Year the 'Tie/Co-Winners' strike gets P(tie) = historical co-winner frequency in the award's own history (to be counted from its published list) shrunk toward the pooled frequency across comparable awards with k=10 awards.
free_sources: Pro Football Reference awards and voting (free_scrape)

nfl.draft_qb_class_model.label: Draft positional-selection model (QB class order, draft order, team need and trade-up)
nfl.draft_qb_class_model.mechanism: The k-th quarterback drafted is determined by the ranked order in which teams on the clock select QBs, which depends on consensus prospect rank, the order of picks of QB-needy teams, and trades that move teams up.
nfl.draft_qb_class_model.rationale: Draft contracts such as 'player X is the 3rd quarterback drafted' are order statistics over a small class (about 8 to 14 QBs drafted per year), where a single early-round team's need and a trade-up change the rank of all later QBs. The generic consensus-board input gives one prospect's rank but not the joint ordering that the count-based contract settles on.
nfl.draft_qb_class_model.measurement: Plackett-Luce ordering model over the QBs in the class: utility_j = -beta*ln(consensus_rank_j) + gamma*need(team on the clock) with consensus_rank an average of at least 5 public big boards (time-stamped; weights proportional to each board's historical rank-correlation with actual draft order), beta and gamma fit by maximum likelihood on 2010-2025 drafts (about 180 QBs), team need = 1 if the current starter contract expires within one year or the starter's EPA per play is below the league 25th percentile; draft order from the final standings and traded picks. Simulate 20,000 drafts including a trade-up probability for QB-needy teams outside the top 5 (estimated from the 2010-2025 share of QBs taken before their consensus slot, shrunk with k=5). Report P(QB j is the k-th QB selected) and P(QB j drafted in the top n). As-of: refreshed after the combine, pro days, and each time a credible insider reports intentions; final run at draft start. Betting or market odds are excluded and used as benchmarks only.
free_sources: public big-board and mock draft aggregator pages
team standings and traded-pick lists (nflverse, league site)

nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.label: Broadcast and event role assignment model (announced crews, contracts and appearance history)
nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.mechanism: A named person performs a role in a named network's broadcast only if the network assigns them to that event and they appear, which follows announced crew sheets, multi-year talent contracts and prior appearance frequency.
nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.rationale: KXNFLROLE settles on whether a person performs as an on-air analyst in a specific network broadcast in a window; this is a staffing decision with a mostly public paper trail (crew announcements, contract news), not an athletic outcome, and it needs base rates by role type rather than a vote or a season model.
nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.measurement: P(role) = P(person on the network's announced crew for at least one qualifying event in the window) x P(appears given assigned). Crew assignment is estimated by logistic regression on the person's number of qualifying events in each of the previous 3 seasons (with weights 0.5, 0.3, 0.2), contract end year, the network's announced lead-crew roster (binary), and whether the event is the network's lead broadcast; P(appears | assigned) = 1 minus the withdrawal rate (illness, conflicts) from the past 5 seasons, shrunk with k=10 events toward 0.97. As-of: each network crew press release and contract report, stamped to the hour; before an announcement the prior-season frequency is used.
free_sources: network press releases and crew announcements (free)

nfl.injury_return_timeline.label: Injury-specific return-time distribution
nfl.injury_return_timeline.mechanism: Time from injury onset to first game played, by body part and severity.
nfl.injury_return_timeline.rationale: Whether a player appears in week k depends on the recovery clock; type-specific survival curves replace an undifferentiated 'injured' flag.
nfl.injury_return_timeline.measurement: Kaplan-Meier or Weibull survival of games missed by (body part, injury report wording, surgical or not, position group) from 2009-2025 injury reports, censored at season end; hazard of return by week since onset; shrink to position-pooled curves with k=10 cases; as-of report date; output P(returns by game k).

nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.label: Practice-sequence and designation to play-probability calibration
nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.mechanism: Calibrated P(plays | Wednesday, Thursday, Friday practice status, designation, position, team, week).
nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.rationale: The mapping is team-specific: some teams use Questionable for near-certain players, others reserve it for coin flips; position matters because linemen and skill players differ.
nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.measurement: Hierarchical logistic regression of played (>=1 snap) on practice-sequence pattern (e.g., DNP-LP-FP), designation, position group, days of rest, and team random effect with shrinkage prior (tau fitted); training 2012-2025 injury reports with vintages; as-of each report time; output P(play) with credible interval.
free_sources: nflverse injuries (practice status, report status) and snap counts
NFL official injury reports (own_capture for timing)

nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.label: Healthy-inactive and rest base rates by role and coach
nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.mechanism: Probability that a healthy player is inactive due to coach choice (rest, discipline, 46-man cut).
nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.rationale: About a fifth of inactives are healthy; rest decisions are concentrated in weeks 17-18 and for veterans on clinched teams.
nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.measurement: From inactive lists and injury report absences (no injury listed) 2015-2025: rate by position, age band, depth slot, team clinch status, coach; shrink to league by k=15 player-games; as-of the week.

nfl.qb_change_hazard.label: Starting-QB change hazard (benching or promotion) by week
nfl.qb_change_hazard.mechanism: Per-week hazard that the depth chart lists a different starting QB than the previous week.
nfl.qb_change_hazard.rationale: First-start contracts are about the hazard of leaving the starter's role; incumbent performance, team record and the next QB's draft capital govern it, and the weeks right after the bye are higher hazard.
nfl.qb_change_hazard.measurement: Discrete-time logistic hazard on QB-weeks 2010-2025: incumbent EPA+CPOE composite vs prior, team record, turnovers, week since bye, challenger draft round and contract, coach tenure, owner pressure; shrink coefficients with ridge; output weekly h and cumulative probability over contract window excluding byes; as-of report date.

nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.label: P(at least one snap | active) by role
nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.mechanism: Probability that an active player plays at least one snap (including or excluding special teams) by depth slot and script.
nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.rationale: The contract requires a snap, so an active emergency QB or deep rotation player may resolve NO; the base rate varies by role.
nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.measurement: From snap counts 2016-2025: fraction of active player-games with at least one offensive, defensive or special-teams snap by position and depth slot; shrinkage k=10 games; adjust for spread (blowouts raise backup snaps); output separate probabilities with and without special-teams snaps.

nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.label: Depth-chart publication mechanics and lag by team
nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.mechanism: How and when each team publishes its official depth chart and how 'starter' is encoded.
nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.rationale: First-start contracts settle on the published chart; teams differ on publication day and encoding (or-designations), so the label can differ from who actually starts.
nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.measurement: Per team-week from archive of depth charts (team websites and nflverse depth_charts), record publication weekday, whether an 'or' slot is used, change relative to prior week; compute P(chart lists a different QB1 than the actual week's starter); as-of week.

nfl.roster_designation_constraints.label: Roster designation and league-rule hard constraints (IR, PUP, NFI, suspension)
nfl.roster_designation_constraints.mechanism: Mandatory minimum absence lengths and eligibility windows from the IR, PUP, NFI and suspension rules.
nfl.roster_designation_constraints.rationale: A player on IR cannot return for four games; suspensions have fixed lengths; these hard constraints dominate the injury recovery curve in the short run.
nfl.roster_designation_constraints.measurement: Rule table by season (IR minimum games, designated-to-return count, practice window 21 days, PUP and NFI rules, suspension length) joined to the player's status on each date; output earliest eligible game and the probability mass allowed by rule; as-of transaction wire.

nfl.non_roster_return_status.label: Non-roster status transition model (retired, free agent, suspended or unsigned player returning to play)
nfl.non_roster_return_status.mechanism: A player who is not on an active roster can only take a snap after a chain of discrete events: ending retirement or suspension, signing with a team, passing a physical, and being activated, each with its own timing and decision-maker.
nfl.non_roster_return_status.rationale: The injury-report-to-inactive-list mechanism does not apply to a retired or unsigned player such as the sampled KXNFLWEEKCOMPETE subject (a player outside any current roster); the live contracts KXNFLRETURN and KXNFLNEXTTEAM are also status-transition events, so a separate model with reference classes for comebacks is required.
nfl.non_roster_return_status.measurement: P(plays in week w) = P(contract signed by the week-w roster deadline) x P(activated and takes a snap | signed). Estimate the first factor as a discrete-time hazard on retired and unsigned veterans 2000-2025 (age, years since last game, Pro Bowl count, stated intent in the previous 12 months as a binary flag, team contract interest reported by named insiders as a binary flag with a timestamp, days to the target week), with ridge shrinkage and a Beta(1, 19) prior for the base comeback rate; estimate the second from signing-to-first-snap lags of mid-season veteran signings (median lag in weeks, shrunk with k=8 signings). For NEXTTEAM contracts output P(team k) by multinomial logit on prior-team cap space, position need and reported interest, with a 'retires or no team' category. As-of: each transaction-wire timestamp and insider report time.
free_sources: league transactions page and Pro-Football-Reference transactions (free_scrape)

nfl.qb_challenger_prior.label: Incumbent-versus-challenger quarterback value gap (draft-capital prior for unproven QBs)
