nfl.qb_challenger_prior.mechanism: The expected performance gap between the incumbent starter and a challenger drives benching and promotion decisions; for rookies and players with few dropbacks the challenger's value rests on a prior built from draft position.
nfl.qb_challenger_prior.rationale: The first-start contracts (KXNFLFIRSTSTART, KXNFLDEBUT) are about a named unproven QB overtaking an incumbent, and the incumbent's in-season EPA alone ignores how good the challenger is expected to be; teams that spent a high pick tolerate a shorter leash for the incumbent.
nfl.qb_challenger_prior.measurement: gap_w = EPA_incumbent_w - EPA_challenger_prior_w where EPA_incumbent_w is the incumbent's opponent-adjusted EPA per dropback over the last 8 games with a prior of league-average QB EPA at weight 150 dropbacks, and EPA_challenger_prior_w = a regression of first-3-season EPA per dropback on log draft pick (2000-2025 QBs with at least 150 dropbacks) blended with the challenger's own preseason and in-game dropbacks using weight n/(n+150). Pick number enters as a continuous slope, undrafted as pick 260. Output the gap and its SD for the discrete-time logistic hazard in nfl.qb_change_hazard. As-of: after each game, with bye weeks excluded from the exposure count.

nfl.qb_expected_pass_td.label: QB expected passing TDs (xPassTD) from dropback-level location and target
nfl.qb_expected_pass_td.mechanism: Sum over a QB's dropbacks of the probability that the attempt becomes a TD given field position, down, distance, target type and defensive look.
nfl.qb_expected_pass_td.rationale: Realized TD counts are noisy; a location-based expectation separates opportunity from finishing luck and gives the per-attempt TD rate that actually predicts forward counts.
nfl.qb_expected_pass_td.measurement: Fit a logistic model P(pass TD | yardline_100, down, ydstogo, air_yards bucket, pass_location, offense_personnel, defenders_in_box) on 2006+ pass attempts using pbp-only fields (yardline_100, down, ydstogo, air_yards bucket, pass_location) and, as an upgrade fitted only on the participation era (about 2016+), offense_personnel and defenders_in_box, which are not available for earlier seasons; for each QB, expected TDs per attempt = average over his attempts last 700 attempts (half-life 350 attempts); shrink to team-level rate with k=300 attempts; ratio of actual to expected regressed 70% to 1.0; as-of previous game.
free_sources: nflverse ff_opportunity expected pass TD columns (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for exact fields)

nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.label: Team goal-to-go and inside-20 pass rate by zone and down
nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.mechanism: Share of snaps that are dropbacks in the zones 20-11, 10-6, 5-1 yards, by down and score state, by team and coach.
nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.rationale: The share of team TDs that are passing depends on goal-to-go play-calling; it varies from about 30% to 70% across teams and drives the QB's TD count more than the total.
nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.measurement: From pbp 2 seasons (half-life 20 games): dropback rate in each zone by down and score_differential bucket; coach random effect shrunk with k=25 plays per zone; blend for new coordinator with league prior; output expected passing TDs fraction of team TDs given the team's red-zone trips; as-of previous game.

nfl.qb_attempt_forecast.label: QB pass-attempt count distribution by script and environment
nfl.qb_attempt_forecast.mechanism: Forecast distribution of the QB's attempts using team plays, pass rate conditional on expected state, sacks, wind and QB participation.
nfl.qb_attempt_forecast.rationale: Attempts are the exposure for TDs, completions and INTs; ignoring their conditional distribution across scripts mixes games where the QB throws 25 times and 45 times.
nfl.qb_attempt_forecast.measurement: Negative binomial regression of QB attempts on expected team plays, expected spread bucket (model-based), neutral PROE, wind>15 flag, dome, opponent run-defence rank, with team random effects; 2015+ QB-games; output mean and dispersion; adjust for P(QB pulled) using nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard; as-of start of week.

nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.label: QB blowout pull and early-exit hazard
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.mechanism: Probability that the QB leaves the game early because of a lopsided score or injury, as a function of lead and time.
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.rationale: Protected and standard contracts differ on pulls; a QB pulled up 28 in the fourth quarter has truncated counts and the protected contract voids.
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.measurement: From pbp 2010-2025: hazard that the starting QB's last snap occurs before game end, by lead size and clock; coach random effect (k=8 blowout games); combine with in-game injury hazard by QB mobility; P(plays 2H) and P(pulled with lead>=21 before end of Q3); as-of start of week.

nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.label: Opponent defence interception propensity, QB-quality adjusted
nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.mechanism: Opponent's interceptions per attempt over expectation given the quality of QBs faced and pressure generated.
nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.rationale: Interception counts by defence are heavily luck; the skill component (ball skills, safety range) must be separated from the pressure effect and from opposing QB quality.
nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.measurement: Interceptions per attempt faced by the defence, adjusted by opposing QB turnover-worthy rate (season), pressure rate faced and pass depth; regress to league mean with k=350 attempts; recency half-life 12 games; as-of previous game.
free_sources: PFF/Sports Info Solutions charting (paid) for turnover-worthy throws

nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.label: Season and career passing-TD accrual model with games and aging
nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.mechanism: Projected remaining TDs given per-game rate, games remaining, availability and aging curve.
nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.rationale: Season (40+) and career markets are sums over games; the distribution of games played and a QB's age-related change in TD rate matter as much as the per-game mean.
nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.measurement: Per-game TD mean from nfl.qb_expected_pass_td and attempt forecast, trend by age (QB aging curve estimated 2000-2025: attempts flat then decline from age 35, TD rate regressed), games remaining from schedule minus byes, availability from injury hazard (QB games missed per season by age and mobility, beta prior); simulate season totals with negative binomial game counts; as-of previous game.

nfl.red_zone_target_quality.label: Red-zone catcher quality and availability (contested-catch and size-weighted target value)
nfl.red_zone_target_quality.mechanism: The probability that a red-zone or goal-to-go throw becomes a touchdown depends on who is the target: tall, contested-catch receivers and tight ends convert short throws at higher rates than slot receivers, so QB touchdown counts depend on the supporting cast.
nfl.red_zone_target_quality.rationale: nfl.skill_avail captures absences but not the quality level of red-zone catchers; a QB with a dominant red-zone target has a higher per-attempt TD rate independent of his own skill, and a team's passing-TD count is lost when that player is out or replaced.
nfl.red_zone_target_quality.measurement: For each team-week, rz_target_quality = sum over players of (share of team targets inside the opponent 20 over the last 12 games, half-life 6 games) x (player's red-zone catch rate over expected, shrunk to the league mean with k=20 red-zone targets) x (availability weight from the active/inactive status at the as-of time); standardise across teams within season; output the team value and the value lost when the top red-zone target is replaced by the next on the chart. As-of: after the previous game and updated at the inactive list.

nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.label: Quarterback benching rule: margin and clock at which the starter is pulled
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.mechanism: Head-coach-specific rule for resting the starter in lopsided games, which removes dropbacks on the winning side and sets the zero-attempt atom after halftime for the protected variant.
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.rationale: Existing exit-risk input treats injury and benching together. For a quarterback on a heavy favourite, benching is a coach habit tied to margin and minutes remaining, not a physical hazard; it lowers the top rungs even when the pre-game model expects a high-yardage game and decides whether a protected contract refunds.
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.measurement: For each head coach, over the last 3 seasons (min 8 qualifying games, shrink toward league mean with k=6 games), record the lead (points) and game-clock minute at which the starter QB's last snap occurred in games decided by 17+; fit a logistic: P(starter pulled | lead, minutes_remaining). Output pre-game: P(pull before Q4 ends) = integral over simulated margin paths, as-of the last pre-game depth chart. Unit: probability and expected minutes lost.
free_sources: nflverse play-by-play (last QB snap per game)

nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.label: Dropback-to-attempt leakage rate (sack, scramble, spike, kneel) for the QB-offence pair
nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.mechanism: Share of dropbacks that never become passing attempts because they end in sacks, scrambles or clock-stopping spikes.
nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.rationale: Passing yards credit only attempts and official QB yardage is gross, so the attempts count is dropbacks times (1 - leakage). Leakage is the interaction of the opponent pressure rate and this passer's tendency to escape or hold the ball; two quarterbacks with equal EPA per dropback can differ by 4-6 attempts per game from this alone.
nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.measurement: Per QB over his last 17 starts, time-decayed with half-life 8 games: (sacks + scrambles + spikes) / dropbacks, shrunk toward the offence-level rate with k=150 dropbacks. Pre-game forecast = QB rate adjusted by opponent pressure rate allowed relative to league (log-odds additive), capped to 3 sd. Units: fraction of dropbacks.
free_sources: nflverse play-by-play: qb_scramble, sack, qb_spike, qb_kneel flags

nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.label: Route-weighted receiving-corps quality for the projected active set
nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.mechanism: Aggregate of expected separation, catch-probability-over-expected and yards after catch over expected across the receivers and backs projected to run routes, weighted by projected route share.
nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.rationale: The passer's yield depends on who catches the ball. A binary flag for WR1 out ignores that a replacement with a much lower route share and weaker separation changes yards per attempt, and that the effect depends on the whole route tree. Need a number that moves when a name changes on the inactive list.
nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.measurement: For each receiver, rolling 12-game route-weighted separation, catch rate over expected and YACOE, shrunk toward position mean with k=60 targets; corps score = sum over projected active receivers of projected route share x player score, where route shares are redistributed from the declared inactive list using the last 3 games' conditional shares. Units: standardized yards per attempt over league mean, as-of inactive list time (about 90 minutes pre-kick) or last practice report.
free_sources: nflverse participation and FTN charting where available
NFL Next Gen Stats public tables (separation, cushion, YAC over expected)

nfl.long_completion_tail_rate.label: Long-completion (20+, 40+ yard) rate and its team-opponent matchup
nfl.long_completion_tail_rate.mechanism: Probability per attempt of a 20+ or 40+ yard completion, which creates the right tail of a quarterback's yardage total.
nfl.long_completion_tail_rate.rationale: The over-rung probability for 300+ is governed by tail events, not the mean. Explosive-pass rate is more erratic than yards per attempt, depends on deep-target share, pass protection time and the opponent's safety play, and is the first thing wind removes.
nfl.long_completion_tail_rate.measurement: Per QB-offence, rate of completions >=20 and >=40 yards per attempt over the last 20 games with half-life 10 games, shrunk with k=200 attempts; opponent factor = opponent's allowed explosive-pass rate relative to league over last 12 games with k=150 attempts; combined multiplicatively on log scale; wind above 15 mph applied as a separate multiplier from nfl.weather_pit. Output: expected count of 20+ and 40+ completions and a compound-Poisson tail for yards.

nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.label: Own-rating margin and total prior for the game-state distribution (market-free)
nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.mechanism: Builds the distribution of the expected score path from the team's own offence and defence ratings, home edge and starter quarterback status, so nfl.script is fed without any sportsbook spread or total.
nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.rationale: nfl.script's catalog measurement integrates over a margin distribution centred on the point spread; that makes the volume driver an echo of the market. The margin and total centre must come from own opponent-adjusted EPA ratings so it can be compared against Kalshi prices rather than copied from them.
nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.measurement: Expected margin = (off_epa_A - def_epa_B) - (off_epa_B - def_epa_A) per play x expected plays per team (nfl.pace), plus a home-field constant fitted on 2015-2025 games (about 1.5 points, refit yearly) and a starter-QB adjustment from nfl.qb_efficiency versus the replacement backup; EPA inputs use a 10-game exponential half-life (about 6 games) shrunk to league mean with k=6 games, opponent-adjusted by ridge. Expected total = sum of the two team expected plays x points per play. Margin sd = 13.0 points, total sd = 9.5 points, re-estimated from own residuals. As-of: last game before kickoff, QB and injury status at the latest inactive list. Contains no spread_line, total_line or moneyline.

nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.label: With/without target redistribution matrix for the projected inactive set
nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.mechanism: Conditional split of routes, targets and air yards among remaining receivers when a given teammate does not play.
nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.rationale: The generic target-competition input says teammates matter; what a model needs is the share each remaining player gains when a specific player is out, because slot, outside and tight end absorbers behave differently and the gain is not proportional to current share.
nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.measurement: For each team-season from 2018, compute each receiver's target share and TPRR in games without teammate X versus with X (X = a top-3 target earner), requiring at least 4 games without X over the last 3 seasons, else use a position-role template pooled across teams (shrink with k=40 targets). Apply to the projected inactive list at the last available timestamp. Output: expected target share vector summing to 1 and a standard error per receiver.

nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.label: Player reception-length distribution (air yards plus yards after catch), incl. longest-play probability
nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.mechanism: Empirical distribution of this receiver's yards per reception and probability that any single reception exceeds 20, 30, 40 and 60 yards.
nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.rationale: The longest-reception market and the escalator tails need the upper tail of catch lengths, which differs from the mean yards per catch; YAC-heavy slot players and deep WRs have the same mean and very different tails.
nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.measurement: For each receiver, take receptions from the last 24 games (min 40; pooled to position-alignment template with k=30 receptions otherwise), fit a log-normal/ Pareto splice at the 85th percentile; then P(longest >= x | N catches) = 1 - F(x)^N with N drawn from the projected receptions distribution. Opponent factor = opposing defence's allowed explosive-reception rate vs league (k=120). Units: probabilities for each strike.

nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.label: Defensive target funnel: share of opponent targets allowed by alignment and position
nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.mechanism: Fraction of opposing pass targets a defence allows to WRs (slot and outside), TEs and RBs, relative to league and adjusted for the offences it faced.
nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.rationale: Defence-versus-position yield tells how efficient receivers are against a defence but not how many targets it sends to each group, which sets a receiver's share before efficiency matters.
nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.measurement: For each defence: over the last 12 games (half-life 6 games) compute target shares by alignment, adjusted for opponent offence's usual share using a ridge model (alpha tuned by cross-season validation); shrink toward league with k=100 targets. Output: log ratio of expected share vs the receiver's usual share. Needs alignment tags from charting data.
free_sources: nflverse FTN charting (limited alignment fields), play-by-play

nfl.qb_target_concentration.label: Quarterback target concentration and first-read lean
nfl.qb_target_concentration.mechanism: Gini or Herfindahl of the quarterback's targets across his receivers, plus the share to the primary read in the last 20 starts.
nfl.qb_target_concentration.rationale: A quarterback who locks onto one receiver gives that receiver both a higher mean and a higher variance, and when the primary receiver is out the concentration determines how widely targets spread.
nfl.qb_target_concentration.measurement: For each quarterback, compute target-share Herfindahl over his last 20 starts (half-life 10 games, min 200 targets; shrink to team-level with k=150 targets) and the primary receiver's share. Apply to the receiver under study as a multiplier on expected target share relative to neutral dispersion: share_adj = share x (1 + b x (conc - league_conc)) with b estimated by out-of-sample regression.

nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.label: Late-lead clock-killing carries: expected volume and yield by back
nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.mechanism: Number of carries a runner takes while his team leads in the second half and their yards per carry, which differ from neutral-game carries because defences stack boxes and runs are designed to burn clock.
nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.rationale: Volume rises for favourites but each carry yields less, so counting these carries at the average yards per carry overstates yardage, and the carries often go to a different back than the one who carried in neutral situations.
nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.measurement: Using play-by-play from the last 3 seasons, for each team compute carries per game in second-half states with lead >= 7 by back, and yards per carry in those states (shrink toward the league leading-state yield with k=25 carries). Forecast = integral over pre-game margin distribution of lead-state carries x lead-state yield, using the back depth chart at the last report. Units: carries and yards per carry.

nfl.run_scheme_vs_front_matchup.label: Run-scheme versus defensive front match by gap and direction
nfl.run_scheme_vs_front_matchup.mechanism: Matches the offence's distribution of runs by gap and direction (inside zone, outside zone, power) and blocking scheme with the defence's yards-allowed by the same gap and its front alignment.
nfl.run_scheme_vs_front_matchup.rationale: Team-level rush defence hides that a front may be soft to the outside and stout inside; the runner's yardage depends on how often the offence attacks the weak gap.
nfl.run_scheme_vs_front_matchup.measurement: For each offence compute share of rushes by run_gap and run_location over the last 16 games (shrink to league with k=60 carries); for each defence compute yards per carry and success rate allowed by the same bins (shrink with k=40). Matchup score = sum over bins of offence share x (defence allowed - league), as expected yards over average per carry. Add nominal front type (odd/even) as a context flag.

nfl.rush_explosive_tail_rate.label: Runner explosive-run rate (10+, 20+) and opponent explosive allowed
nfl.rush_explosive_tail_rate.mechanism: Per-carry probabilities of 10+ and 20+ yard runs for this runner and the matching rate the defence allows.
nfl.rush_explosive_tail_rate.rationale: The 100+ rung is rarely reached through steady 4-yard carries; it needs one or two long runs, and the per-carry explosive probability is a separate parameter with its own persistence and opponent dependence.
nfl.rush_explosive_tail_rate.measurement: For each runner, explosive rate over the last 25 games with half-life 12 games, shrunk to the position-role mean with k=60 carries; opponent factor = defence's allowed 10+ rate vs league over last 16 games (k=100); combine on a log scale; use in a compound simulation of yardage with carries from stage s1-s4. Output: P(10+), P(20+) per carry.

nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.label: Quarterback scramble and designed-run yield conditioned on pressure
nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.mechanism: For a quarterback: probability that a pressured dropback becomes a scramble, yards per scramble and designed-run carries per game by situation.
nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.rationale: For quarterback rushing contracts yardage arises from scrambles under pressure and from scheme, not from handoffs; scramble conversion depends on coverage downfield and on the passer's mobility, and designed runs are a coaching feature.
nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.measurement: For each QB, scrambles per pressured dropback and yards per scramble over the last 24 games (half-life 12), designed-run carries per game from the last 12; shrink with k=80 dropbacks (scramble) and k=5 games (designed). Opponent adjustment: opposing pressure rate (log-odds) and spy/contain tendencies from charting. Output: expected carries and yards with variance. Needs pressure flags from a charting vendor or the sack/hit proxy.

nfl.award_milestone_proximity.label: Milestone and record proximity for each candidate
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.mechanism: Distance of a candidate's projected final total from round-number or record milestones that voters respond to (e.g. 2,000 rushing yards, 5,000 passing yards, 20 sacks, franchise or league records).
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.rationale: Vote probability is not smooth in production: reaching a milestone adds a discrete narrative bump and a record chase draws attention for several weeks, so award probability has a cliff near thresholds.
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.measurement: For each candidate and award, list milestone totals from the last 15 years of winners' stat lines (the 20th percentile of winners' totals for each key stat as threshold); compute probability that projected final total exceeds each threshold from the season-to-date accrual model (rate x remaining games with games-played risk); feature = P(exceed) and distance in games. Rolls forward after each week; units: probability.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference season stats and award voting history

nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.label: Teammate and look-alike candidate vote-splitting penalty
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.mechanism: Reduction in a candidate's vote share caused by another strong candidate with the same team, position or narrative.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.rationale: Plurality voting splits similar support: two quarterbacks on the same team or two edge rushers with similar sack counts take votes from each other, so independent win probabilities overstate the sum and understate a third candidate's chance.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.measurement: From historical AP voting records (last 20 seasons), estimate a Plackett-Luce or Dirichlet model where each candidate's latent score includes a penalty beta x (score of the best same-team or same-position rival); estimate beta by maximum likelihood with candidates having at least one vote; shrink beta toward 0 with a ridge prior (lambda tuned by leave-one-season-out). Output: winner probabilities after the split correction.

nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.label: Rookie opportunity: draft capital, starter status and snap/role share
nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.mechanism: Draft pick number, starter status in Week 1 and cumulative snap share of rookies, plus team context (quarterback, line) that gives opportunities.
nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.rationale: Rookie awards go to rookies who played substantial roles on visible teams; draft capital predicts both opportunity and the voters' prior, and the role is determined by early-season depth charts and injuries ahead of him.
nfl.rookie_opportunity_and_draft_capital.measurement: For each rookie: draft pick (log scale), team depth chart rank at the first week's report, snap share and touches or pressures per game over the season, shrunk with k=3 games; feature = expected rest-of-season production given role, based on a regression of final production on first-6-week role and draft slot over 2010-2025 rookies.
free_sources: nflverse draft picks and snap counts

nfl.award_month_window_games.label: Monthly award window: games, byes and stat accrual inside the calendar window
nfl.award_month_window_games.mechanism: Number of games each candidate's team plays in the contract's calendar month and the candidate's stat production within that window.
nfl.award_month_window_games.rationale: Monthly awards are decided on three to five games, so a team on a bye, a rest day or a Thursday game changes the sample; a candidate with five games has more chances than one with three.
nfl.award_month_window_games.measurement: For each award month, from the league schedule: games per team in the window (3, 4 or 5); expected stats per game from the candidate's role and an opponent adjustment; window total = sum over games; standard deviation scaled by sqrt(games) with game-level variance from the player's last 20 games. Output probability that the candidate leads the window at his position.

nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.label: Coach surprise: wins above own pre-season expectation
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.mechanism: Team win total minus the expected wins from a pre-season rating built without betting-market inputs (own roster and last-year efficiency prior).
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.rationale: Coach of the Year is a vote for surprise rather than quality, so the relevant measure is outcome minus prior expectation; using a sportsbook win total would import a market price as an input, so the prior must be from the model's own rating.
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.measurement: Pre-season expected wins = sum over remaining games of own win probability from team rating (roster continuity regression of last-year EPA, QB change, strength of schedule); surprise = (projected final wins from standings simulation) - pre-season expected wins; add division title and playoff seed bonuses based on historical winners; units: wins above expectation.

nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.label: Voter exposure: primetime games, national attention and public straw polls
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.mechanism: Count of primetime and national games for the candidate's team so far and standing in published writers' ballots or straw polls from non-market sources.
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.rationale: Voters see the nationally televised games and discuss candidates in public straw polls; this is a signal of voter sentiment distinct from production and is not a market price.
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.measurement: Primetime-game counts and share of the candidate's yards or touchdowns in those games to date; rank in published straw polls (e.g. by members of the voting panel) at each week (rank points via Borda). Combined into one score with weights from historical regression on vote share, as-of each Tuesday; no betting prices or Kalshi quotes used.

nfl.position_peer_production_index.label: Cross-position production index versus peers (offence and defence)
nfl.position_peer_production_index.mechanism: Converts a candidate's season-to-date production into a position-neutral standing among eligible candidates, using EPA-based value for offensive players and a defensive-production composite for defenders.
nfl.position_peer_production_index.rationale: The record's production stage relied on WEAK inputs and one QB-only input, so DPOY, DROY and OPOY (skill positions) had no calibrated production measure. Voters compare a sack leader with a coverage corner, so a within-position percentile is needed; it must also be shrunk for small samples early in the season.
nfl.position_peer_production_index.measurement: Offensive candidates: EPA contributed per game (QB: EPA+CPOE composite from nfl.qb_efficiency; RB/WR/TE: receiving or rushing EPA plus yards over expected per touch) converted to z-score versus the 2015-2025 distribution of the same position at the same week of season. Defenders: composite z of sacks per game, pressures per game (if available) and QB hits, interceptions plus passes defensed, tackles for loss, and forced fumbles with weights 0.35/0.25/0.15/0.15/0.10 (weights are assumptions to be fit to past DPOY vote share); shrink toward position mean with k=5 games; ranks within the eligible pool (rookies only for rookie awards); as-of the last completed week. Output: rank and z-gap to the next candidate.
free_sources: nflverse weekly player stats (sacks, QB hits, interceptions, passes defended, TFL)

nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.label: Rest-of-season statistical projection to the ballot cutoff
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.mechanism: Projects each candidate's final regular-season totals by adding expected remaining-game production to banked totals, with a games-played hazard.
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.rationale: Awards are voted on final-season body of work, and Kalshi prices trade in October to January while about half the games remain; ranking by banked stats ignores that a candidate on a bye or with a tough schedule will fall behind. The projection is for production rank, not a price.
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.measurement: Projected total = banked total + sum over remaining games g of P(plays g) x expected per-game rate_g, where the per-game rate is a 50/50 blend of season-to-date per-game rate and a 3-year prior (shrunk with k=6 games), scaled by opponent defence adjustment from nfl.schedule_strength (+-10 percent cap) and by P(plays g) from nfl.games_played_dist; uncertainty from a negative-binomial per-game sd fitted on 2015-2025. As-of: before the next kickoff window; cutoff = last regular-season game (ballot close date assumed at the end of the regular season, unverified, see u3).

nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.label: Role-regime change hazard (trade, teammate injury, coordinator change)
nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.mechanism: Probability per week that a player's share of targets, carries or snaps shifts materially because of an event outside his own performance.
nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.rationale: Season projections assume the current role persists; events that rewrite a depth chart or play-calling are the main source of large forecast errors and do not appear in per-game variance.
nfl.role_regime_change_hazard.measurement: From 2012-2025 weekly data, define a regime shift as a change of at least 25 percent in a 4-game rolling usage share relative to the prior 4 games; estimate hazard per week by event type (teammate injury, trade, coordinator change, rookie return) with logistic regression, shrunk with k=20 events per type; apply to each contender conditional on the current team state; output expected share distribution (mixture) for the remaining games.
free_sources: nflverse weekly stats, rosters, transactions (roster moves)

nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.label: Within-season persistence of per-game rate (variance components)
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.mechanism: Decomposition of per-game output variance into a persistent player-season component and a game-level noise component.
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.rationale: Season-sum variance is sqrt(n) times game sd only if games are independent; role persistence makes the sum more dispersed, so the probability of reaching distant rungs is larger than an independent model says.
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.measurement: For each statistic and position fit a mixed model on 2012-2025 player-games: y_game = u_player-season + e_game, with u from a normal distribution and e from a count distribution; estimate the ratio sigma_u / sigma_e and the ICC by position and stat; apply to project season total variance = n x Var(e) + n^2 x Var(u) over remaining games; use the current-season estimate of u as the posterior mean with shrinkage proportional to games played.

nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.label: Clinched-seed rest: expected snap fraction of starters in the final two weeks
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.mechanism: Probability and magnitude of reduced snaps for starters in Week 17-18 when seeds or division titles are clinched.
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.rationale: In the final weeks teams with nothing to play for rest key starters, which truncates cumulative totals just when leader races are decided; the effect depends on the coach's history and on the clinch state.
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.measurement: For each team, compute the probability of each clinch state by Week 16 from the standings simulation; from 2015-2025, estimate expected snap fraction in Weeks 17-18 for starters by position as a function of state (clinched top seed, clinched any seed, eliminated), coach-specific rest history (shrink with k=2 occasions), and player age; output expected fraction of normal snaps and its distribution.

nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.label: Pairwise covariance of remaining output among contenders
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.mechanism: Covariance of remaining-season output between contenders sharing a team, position room or quarterback.
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.rationale: Leader probability involves the probability that one exceeds the other, so independence overstates the probability of both being high; teammates' rushing is negatively linked, and passing and receiving of a QB and his top receiver positively.
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.measurement: From 2012-2025 player-seasons, estimate residual correlation between remaining-season output of pairs (same team same stat; QB-WR pairs; RB-RB) after removing season-level means, using the last 8 weeks as the test window; shrink pairwise correlation to the category average with k=30 pairs; use in a multivariate normal or copula simulation of the contender field.

nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.label: Distribution of the weekly leader's value by position and statistic
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.mechanism: Baseline distribution of the single-game maximum over all players of a position in a given week and the number of near-miss contenders.
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.rationale: The weekly leader market is decided by the top of a very large field; the winner's threshold, not the favourite's mean, sets the chance, and the leader's value is heavy-tailed.
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.measurement: For each position and statistic, from 2010-2025 weeks collect the weekly maximum and top-5 values; fit a generalized extreme value distribution by position; condition on number of games in the week (Thursday, Monday, bye-heavy weeks) and weather. Output P(player i is the weekly max) via simulation of the active-player field with player-specific distributions.

nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.label: Shared team-rating uncertainty (posterior sd) carried across all games
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.mechanism: Posterior standard deviation of each team's latent rating, applied as a common draw across all of that team's games in a simulation.
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.rationale: If every game is simulated at a fixed rating, win totals are too concentrated and tail probabilities for 4-win or 13-win teams are underestimated; the shared error is the main reason season win-total distributions are wider than binomial.
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.measurement: Prior sd = 4.0 points of margin rating at the preseason (assumption: preseason win-total errors have sd about 2.9 wins against a binomial sd of about 2.1, implying a rating sd near 4 points; re-estimate from residuals of own preseason ratings against final ratings over 2002-2025); posterior sd after n games = 1/sqrt(1/prior_sd^2 + n/s^2) where the game-level residual standard deviation is 13.5 points, so s^2 = 13.5^2 = 182.25 points^2. Sample one team-level strength draw per simulation and keep it across all remaining games. Output: sd by team and week.

nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.label: Team-specific quarterback scenario tree and rating drop to the backup
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.mechanism: Expected loss in team rating, in points, when the starting quarterback is replaced by the depth-chart backup, and the probability distribution of missed games.
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.rationale: Quarterback change is the largest swing in team rating, and the size of the drop varies from one point for teams with a competent backup to ten points for teams with a replacement-level one.
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.measurement: For each team, rating drop = (QB1 value - QB2 value) in points, where QB value = career-regressed EPA per dropback prior x dropbacks x conversion (about 0.2 points of margin per 0.01 EPA per dropback per game, from regression), shrunk to league mean with k=300 dropbacks; missed-game distribution from historical QB games missed by age and injury history (negative binomial); scenario tree: QB1 all games, partial, absent. Output expected wins lost and a distribution.

nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.label: Direct-competitor leverage: remaining games among teams contending for the same slots
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.mechanism: Matrix of remaining games between teams whose division or wild-card outcomes are linked, with each game's swing in the target contract's probability.
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.rationale: Games among rivals are zero-sum for the division and seed contract, so they move probabilities by roughly twice as much as other games, and the head-to-head tiebreaker also locks in earlier results.
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.measurement: In each weekly simulation, for each remaining game compute the change in P(contract) between simulated worlds where each team wins (leverage = |P(win)-P(loss)| x game probability uncertainty); aggregate to team-level remaining leverage by division and wild-card group; add head-to-head results to date as first-tiebreak state. Output: leverage score per game and per team.

nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.label: Full-strength playoff rating versus season-average rating
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.mechanism: Team rating computed on games with the current starting lineup (healthy QB, lines, defence) excluding games with rested starters or garbage time.
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.rationale: Regular-season averages include injuries that have healed and rested-starter games in Weeks 17-18, which bias the rating used for playoffs and title futures.
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.measurement: Compute opponent-adjusted efficiency (EPA/play margin) over games where the current starting QB and at least 80 percent of current starters (by snap weight) played, excluding Week 18 rested-starter games and fourth-quarter garbage time (win probability >95 percent); shrink to the season average with k=5 games; output rating in points of margin and the difference from season average as an adjustment for playoff-round probabilities.

nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.label: First-overall-pick race: bottom of standings, strength-of-schedule tiebreak and pick ownership
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.mechanism: Distribution of the team that ultimately makes the first pick, from the worst-record contest with its tiebreak and from ownership of traded picks.
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.rationale: The first-pick contract depends on who has the worst record, the tiebreak for ties (strength of schedule rather than team strength) and whether the pick has been traded, so it is an extreme-value problem of losing, not winning.
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.measurement: Simulate final records, take the minimum-wins team with the league's draft-order tiebreak (lower strength of schedule gets the higher pick, as an assumption flagged SOURCE_UNVERIFIED), then map the draft slot owner via a table of traded picks; add a small tanking adjustment (reduced win probability for teams eliminated by Week 12, estimated from history).

nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.label: Own opponent-adjusted team rating with preseason prior (market-free)
nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.mechanism: A Bayesian margin rating per team built only from game results, play-level EPA, roster continuity and quarterback status, with a home-field constant and a preseason prior, used as the latent strength for every futures simulation.
nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.rationale: Every contract in this archetype depends on team strength, and nfl.ratings is built by inverting spreads and totals, which makes it a copy of the market. A rating from results, EPA and roster inputs can be compared with Kalshi prices as an independent estimate; the subtle part is the preseason prior, which dominates in September and October.
nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.measurement: Weekly update: rating_t in points of margin per game from ridge regression of capped game margin (cap 24) on team and opponent indicators, home indicator (home-field constant fitted yearly, about 1.5 points) over all games since the prior season, weights exp(-ln2 x games_ago/10); combine 50/50 with an opponent-adjusted EPA/play margin rating converted to points (points margin per game = EPA/play margin x about 63 plays per team per game, a conversion to be refit yearly). Preseason prior = 0.67 x last season's final rating (one third reversion to zero) + 0.10 points x (returning-production percent above league mean)/10 + starting-QB change adjustment (QB value difference per nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop) with prior sd 4.0 points (assumption to be recalibrated against 2002-2025 final ratings). Posterior sd after n games = 1/sqrt(1/4.0^2 + n/13.5^2) points (13.5 is a standard deviation, so n/182.25). As-of: kickoff of the next game; no spread, total or moneyline enters.
free_sources: nflverse rosters and snap counts for returning production

nfl.drive_result_lattice.label: Drive-result lattice: touchdown, field goal, turnover, punt probabilities by start position
nfl.drive_result_lattice.mechanism: Per-drive probabilities of touchdown, field goal and no score for this offence against this defence conditioned on starting field position and game state.
nfl.drive_result_lattice.rationale: Team points are the convolution of drive outcomes, not a smooth function of EPA per play: two offences with equal EPA can have different touchdown-to-field-goal mixes, and the mixture decides the cluster of the score.
nfl.drive_result_lattice.measurement: From drive-level play-by-play 2016-2025 estimate multinomial logit of drive result on start yard line, offence rating, defence rating, down-and-distance style, with team-level random effects (shrink team deviations with k=10 drives); output P(TD), P(FG), P(none) for each of 11 drives by start-position distribution and compute the discrete points distribution by convolution including 2-point and XP outcomes.

nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.label: Fourth-down go-for-it versus field-goal decision rate and two-point policy
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.mechanism: Coach-specific probability of going for it on fourth down by field position and distance, and of attempting a two-point conversion.
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.rationale: The decision converts a stalled drive into 3 points, 0 points or 7 points; aggressive coaches raise the variance and shift the mean of team totals, and two-point attempts change points per touchdown.
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.measurement: For each head coach over 3 seasons: P(go | yard line bin, distance bin, score and time bin), shrink to model-based optimum with k=15 decisions; two-point attempts per touchdown shrunk with k=10; expected points per stalled drive = P(go) x [conv x 7 + (1-conv) x 0] + (1-P(go)) x P(make FG | distance) x 3; output delta in expected points per game and variance. As-of last completed game.

nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.label: Non-offensive scoring rate: defensive and special-teams points for and against
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.mechanism: Expected points per game from interception returns, fumble returns, kick and punt return touchdowns and safeties credited to the team, and the equivalent against it.
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.rationale: These points enter the team's total independent of offence, and when scored against the team they end drives; ignoring them biases rungs low for teams with opportunistic defences.
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.measurement: Per team, count of defensive and special-teams scoring plays per game over the last 25 games with half-life 12, shrunk heavily toward league (k=40 games) because these events are rare; split into takeaway-driven part (own takeaway rate x return-score probability) and special-teams part; opponent's rate against the team computed symmetrically. Output expected points and probability of at least one such score.
free_sources: nflverse play-by-play (touchdown with td_team differing from posteam, safety flag)

nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.label: Opponent ball-control denial: expected drives and time removed from this offence
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.mechanism: How much the opponent's time of possession, run share and clock usage cut this offence's number of drives relative to its neutral pace.
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.rationale: A team's own tempo says nothing about drives if the opponent holds the ball; the effect depends on the matchup of styles and is not captured by pace alone.
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.measurement: For each opponent compute average seconds per play, run rate in neutral situations and drive length over the last 12 games (half-life 6); expected own drives = league drives x (own-share model) where own share = own pace / (own pace + opponent pace) adjusted by a regression on historical game drive counts; output expected drives for each side and variance. As-of last game.

nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.label: Own-mean team score probability mass function with key-number structure (market-free)
nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.mechanism: Converts the model's own expected points for a team into a discrete integer score distribution that carries the extra mass at 3, 6, 7, 10 and 14, so every rung of the ladder is read from one pmf.
nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.rationale: The catalog score residual is defined around the closing spread and total, and the team-total split is derived from the same lines, so both are market echoes. The key-number lumpiness is real, but it must be fitted around own predicted means; otherwise the model inherits the market's mean and the comparison with Kalshi prices is circular.
nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.measurement: From all regular-season team-games 2010-2025 take the integer final score; bin by the model's own pre-game expected team points (from nfl.drive_result_lattice means; no sportsbook line) in 1-point bins from 10 to 35; fit within each bin a discrete mixture: negative-binomial body (dispersion estimated per bin, roughly sd 9-10 points) plus a kernel-smoothed empirical correction ratio at scores 0,3,6,7,9,10,13,14,16,17,20,21,23,24,27,28 (correction = observed/NB frequency, shrunk to 1 with k=60 team-games per score). Include overtime points in the pmf and also keep a regulation-only pmf, selecting by contract (KXNFLBOTH counts overtime; KXNFLTEAMTOTAL unstated, see u1). Output: P(score >= n) for n in 0..60, as-of the final pre-kickoff mean.

nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.label: Paired team-score covariance from pace, script and weather (market-free)
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.mechanism: Estimates the covariance between the two teams' scores through shared pace, shared weather and the zero-sum score path, so the joint tail for the both-teams-35 contract is not a product of marginals.
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.rationale: Team scores are positively correlated through plays and drives and conditionally negative through script (a leading team slows play and shortens the other side's comeback window). The joint tail P(both >= 35) is a tail of a score pair and is highly sensitive to the correlation sign at high totals.
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.measurement: Using 2010-2025 games compute the residual correlation of the two team scores after subtracting each team's own model mean, in bins of the expected total (own model total from the two means: low <40, mid 40-50, high >50 points), expected plays (nfl.pace) and wind (calm <10 mph, windy >=15 mph); shrink bin correlations toward the pooled value with k=150 games; sample score pairs from a Gaussian copula with the bin correlation over the two nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean marginals; add a home-field and venue shift (nfl.venue, home team mean +1.5 points, dome flag) into each mean. Output: P(both >= 35) and the correlation by bin. As-of: kickoff forecasts.
free_sources: nflverse schedules (final scores, roof, wind, temp)

nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.label: Pass and run EPA split for both offence and defence, opponent-adjusted
nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.mechanism: Separates each side's points production and prevention into pass and rush components so the matchup between an offence's style and the defence's pass and run strengths can be computed.
nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.rationale: Collapsing the opposing defence to one defensive EPA hides whether it is strong against the pass or the run; a pass-heavy offence is hurt by a pass-defence strength and a run-heavy one by a run-defence strength. The split needs both offences and both defences with enough shrinkage.
nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.measurement: For each team compute offensive EPA per dropback and EPA per rush and defensive EPA per dropback faced and per rush faced from 2016-present play-by-play (excluding kneel-downs, spikes and garbage time at win probability above 95 percent), opponent-adjusted by a ridge regression over the last 12 games with exponential half-life 6 games; shrink each component toward the league mean with k=150 plays for pass and k=100 plays for rush. Expected points rate = pass share x (off pass EPA - opponent pass defence EPA) + run share x (off rush EPA - opponent run defence EPA), with pass share from nfl.pace-adjusted neutral pass rate. As-of last completed game.

nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.label: Component and teammate-stack covariance of fantasy points
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.mechanism: Correlation matrix of a player's scoring components (receptions, yards, touchdowns) and between teammates' scores (quarterback-receiver, same-backfield).
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.rationale: Variance of the fantasy total is mostly covariance, and head-to-head, top-N and ladder markets depend on it; a quarterback touchdown pass produces four points for him and six for his receiver, which the sum-of-marginals logic ignores.
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.measurement: From 2012-2025 player-game data compute the correlation between components within a player and between pairs of teammates, by position pair, after removing team-week means; shrink pairwise correlations to position-pair averages with k=80 games; use a Gaussian or t-copula for joint simulation. Output a correlation matrix per game by team and position and variance multipliers for total scores.

nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.label: Play-level expected touchdowns (xTD) from opportunity location
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.mechanism: Sum over a player's carries and targets of the probability that the play scores a touchdown given its yard line, distance to go and air yards.
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.rationale: Touchdowns are the largest fantasy variance source and regress strongly; share of red-zone usage alone is a coarse measure, while a play-level expected touchdown count is a direct estimate of true touchdown rate.
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.measurement: Fit a logistic model on 2016-2025 plays: P(TD | yardline_100, down, ydstogo, play type, air yards, role) for carries and targets, then player xTD per game = sum of play probabilities over the last 12 games with half-life 6, shrunk toward position-role mean with k=4 games; forecast = xTD rate x projected opportunities; compare actual TD minus xTD for regression diagnostics.

nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.label: Sleeper scoring settings, group membership and correction timing
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.mechanism: Mapping from official stats to Sleeper's default full-PPR points, including kicker and bonus rules, the position group each player is assigned to and when Sleeper publishes or corrects totals.
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.rationale: The contract settles on Sleeper's number, not on the league's stat; a player's position group (WR/RB/TE/QB), rookie flag, rounding and timing of the published value determine the outcome and cannot be assumed from another fantasy platform.
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.measurement: Archive Sleeper's scoring settings (points per yard, per touchdown, per reception, kicker table) and each week's published points at game end, at 24 hours and at settlement; flag differences from the standard stat sheet; keep a table of Sleeper position assignment as of the expiration date; compute a score from official stats and compare with the Sleeper value (error in points).

nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.label: Single-game ceiling tail model for any-game highs
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.mechanism: Probability that a player's single-game score exceeds a high threshold (34, 49 points) in a given game, based on per-game distributions with an extreme-value tail.
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.rationale: Season-high contracts depend on rare big games rather than the mean; the maximum of 17 games grows with the log of games and is dominated by touchdown clusters and long plays.
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.measurement: For each player estimate per-game score distribution with a Poisson-touchdown plus compound yardage model (components from stage s2-s4) and a Pareto tail above the 90th percentile fitted on position-level game scores from 2012-2025; P(max over N remaining games >= x) = 1 - prod(1 - p_g(x)) with p_g adjusted for game-specific total and availability; add an upward correlation correction via nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covariance. Output P at several thresholds by remaining games.

nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.label: Weekly full-pool projection grid and correlation by game
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.mechanism: Projected distribution of fantasy points for every player in a position pool in the week, including bye weeks, inactives and game environment, with shared game effects.
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.rationale: Weekly leader and top-5 contracts are decided across the whole pool, so the probability for a listed player depends on how many other strong options play that week, and on shootouts that lift several players together.
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.measurement: For each week and position pool (WR, RB, TE, QB) project every player with at least 5 percent of position snap share: mean and variance from the component model, game environment effect from the own-model projected team points (nfl.off_epa, nfl.def_epa and nfl.pace; never a sportsbook total) shared across the game's players, and a probability of inactivity from the injury vintage; simulate 20,000 weeks to compute P(rank = 1) and P(rank <= 5) for each player including ties at the cutoff (1/N).

nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.label: Count-statistic dispersion by stat and score-state split
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.mechanism: Negative-binomial dispersion parameters and mean multipliers for field goals, sacks, interceptions, rushing attempts and yards by score state and game total.
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.rationale: Thresholds like 4+ field goals or 6+ sacks are tail masses; a Poisson assumption understates them, and dispersion changes with whether the game is a blowout or a close contest.
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.measurement: From 2012-2025 team-games fit, per stat, a negative binomial with mean = opportunities x rate and dispersion k by stat and by score-state bucket (lead>=14, within 7, trail>=14); shrink k toward the league-stat value with a gamma prior (equivalent to 200 team-games); output PMF for each stat given expected mean and state mixture over the pre-game margin distribution.

nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.label: Long field-goal attempt and make model (50+ and 60+ yards), by kicker, venue and weather
nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.mechanism: Expected number of attempts of 55+ and 60+ yards and make probability by distance bin for each kicker, adjusted for altitude, roof and wind.
nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.rationale: The 60+ yard season contract needs the number of attempts (a coaching and game-state decision, usually at the end of halves) and a steeply falling make probability, both with strong venue and kicker dependence.
nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.measurement: Per kicker over his last 3 seasons: make probability by distance bin (50-54, 55-59, 60+) from a logistic regression on distance, altitude, dome and wind with kicker random effect (shrink with k=8 attempts); league attempt rate of 60+ per 100 games adjusted for end-of-half and score state; season expected count = sum over games of attempts x make; for Denver (altitude) add venue multiplier. Output expected count and variance for the league total.

nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.label: Win-streak and undefeated-hazard path model across 32 teams
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.mechanism: Probability distribution of the longest win streak, the week of the last first loss, and the number of ties, from a correlated season simulation with shared rating uncertainty.
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.rationale: Streak and undefeated contracts depend on the sequence of game outcomes and on strength dispersion, not just on win totals; ties break streaks without being losses, and a bye week is an unrecorded week. It is now week 9 of the season, so most of these contracts are partly decided by banked results and the input must carry the current season state, not restart at Week 1.
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.measurement: Do not build a separate simulator: use the single shared season simulator nfl.standings_sim (with the shared rating-uncertainty draw and tie probability of the win-totals record, 0.25 percent per game and rating prior sd of 4.0 points as the shared assumptions) run on REMAINING games only, conditioned on the results already played as of the current week (completed scores, ties, each team's current win streak and undefeated flag, banked 60+ yard field goals and tie count), current injuries and quarterback status. For each of 100,000 runs record: the longest streak (under both tie treatments, see u2) for each team, the week of each team's first loss (ties not losses; same-week first losses tied), season tie count and 60-yard field goal count (banked + simulated), and the worst-to-first indicator; output probabilities for each contract rung.

nfl.primetime_flex_probability.label: Primetime window assignment and flex-scheduling probability
nfl.primetime_flex_probability.mechanism: Number of national-window games a team has in the published schedule and the probability that flexible scheduling adds or removes games before the season ends.
nfl.primetime_flex_probability.rationale: The primetime count is a deterministic function of the schedule apart from flex decisions, which depend on team records and appeal and are announced 6 to 12 days ahead; the count of 5+ games is therefore mostly known at release with a flex-driven change.
nfl.primetime_flex_probability.measurement: From the published schedule, count designated national games by team (Sunday, Monday, Thursday night plus Thanksgiving and Christmas, excluding the Wednesday opener); estimate the probability of a flex in/out per eligible week as a logistic function of team record and previous primetime count from 2023-2025 flex rules (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for current flex rules); expected final count = base + sum of flex probabilities; output PMF.
free_sources: NFL schedule releases and flex announcements

nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.label: Defence sack-count decomposition: opponent dropbacks, pressure rate, conversion
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.mechanism: Expected sacks by this defence equal opponent expected dropbacks times pressure rate times pressure-to-sack conversion, with opposing quarterback's sack avoidance and the offence's pass protection.
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.rationale: The 6+ sacks contract is a tail of a thin count; the mean depends on three multiplicative factors with different regression speeds, and the conversion factor is quarterback specific.
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.measurement: Expected opponent dropbacks from nfl.pace and nfl.script; team pressure rate over last 12 games (half-life 6, shrink k=120 dropbacks); conversion = sacks / pressures with opposing quarterback's career-regressed rate (shrink k=100 pressures) and pass-rusher availability adjustment; E[sacks] = dropbacks x pressure rate x conversion; add overdispersion from the count model. Needs pressure data or a sack-plus-hit proxy.

nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.label: Separate offence and defence scoring rates for season and weekly extremes
nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.mechanism: Estimates each team's points scored and points allowed per game as separate rates with their own uncertainty, so that season scoring extremes and the weekly highest-scoring team can be simulated.
nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.rationale: A single margin rating cannot give points for and points against; the most/least points scored and allowed are extremes over 32 teams that depend on pace, defence and offence separately, and the weekly high score is the maximum of 32 correlated-through-nothing but heavy-tailed team scores. Contracts are priced from the right tail of each team's score distribution.
nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.measurement: For each team compute opponent-adjusted points per game for offence and defence separately: ridge regression of team points on offence and opposing-defence indicators with home indicator, over the last 17 games weighted exp(-ln2 x games_ago/8) with a one-third reversion to league mean before the season (offence k=6 games, defence k=6 games shrink to mean). Simulate remaining games conditioned on points already banked (as of the current week): team season points = banked + sum of simulated scores, each score drawn from a negative binomial with mean from the team's own rates (sd about 9.5 points per team-game, an assumption to refit) and a shared per-team rate draw (sd 1.2 points per game). Weekly high score = max over that week's 32 (or fewer on byes) simulated scores. Output P(team has min/max points scored/allowed) with 1/N ties, and P(team has the weekly high). As-of: after the last completed game.

game_side.mechanism: Moneyline, spread, win-margin and half/period winner markets all price the distribution of final margin: team strength differences (QB-adjusted), home edge, rest and environment shift the mean, while the lattice of NFL scoring (key numbers 3 and 7) and overtime/tie rules shape probabilities at specific lines. The market line already contains most public information, so the model is mainly a calibration and lineup-timing exercise.
game_side.target: Probability that the team wins (moneyline), covers a spread, or the margin falls in a bucket, under the contract's regulation/overtime settlement.

inputs.why: Market-implied and Elo-style team strength is the prior that every other input must add to.
Starter QB status is the largest single swing in margin and resolves late; must be mixed by probability.
Opponent-adjusted offensive efficiency gives the structural mean margin independent of the line.
Defense efficiency completes the team-strength matchup; pass and rush splits matter for specific opponents.
Timestamped injury vintages show which stars are missing at market time.
Short weeks, byes and travel create small systematic margin shifts.
Home-field strength, roof and surface adjust the margin mean.
Wind/precipitation compress scoring and favor the run-heavy/defense-heavy side.
Key-number lattice converts rating differences to probabilities at half-point spreads.
Tie/OT mass differs between regulation-only and including-OT settlement.
Seeding stakes and starter rest change effort and lineup late in the season.
Sharp reference lines are the benchmark; inconsistent Kalshi prices reveal staleness.
Settlement wording (OT, ties, postponement) must match the modelled outcome.
Division games are scouted more heavily; a candidate residual adjustment to margin variance and cover rates.
Defensive injuries alter the defense rating and are knowable from the report vintage.

interactions.hypothesis: QB-status uncertainty interacts with spread size: a backup QB shifts the margin mean and widens the margin SD, so cover probability changes more than moneyline for large spreads.
Wind and cold interact with passing-reliant teams: bad weather lowers the efficiency of pass-first favorites more than run-first teams, narrowing expected margin.
Late-season seeding stakes interact with injury reports: a clinched team with questionable starters has much higher rest probability.

period.mechanism: Half and quarter markets inherit the full-game strength model but add period-specific structure: scripted opening drives, who receives the opening kickoff, two-minute drills before halftime, second-half adjustments and garbage-time. Scoring is smaller and lumpier per period so ties/pushes and key numbers have greater weight; late-game clock management mostly affects only the fourth quarter.
period.target: Points, margin, winner or total in a defined period (first half, quarter), settled per contract wording on ties and overtime.

inputs.why: Team-specific historical quarter/half scoring shares are the base for period totals and margins.
Scripted first drives drive Q1 scoring and the tied-after-Q1 outcome.
Possession order shifts first-quarter and second-half-start scoring.
Two-minute drills produce a disproportionate share of Q2 points.
Lead/trail scripting determines Q3-Q4 pace and how early garbage time begins.
Full-game team strength sets the period margin mean.
Implied team totals from the game total and spread are scaled to the period.
Coaching tendencies (tempo, 4th-down aggression, halftime adjustments) vary the period profile.
Key-number structure for short periods differs from full-game residuals.
Period markets can differ on ties and overtime inclusion.

interactions.hypothesis: Opening possession and opening-drive scripts interact: a team that defers but has a strong scripted offense gets the ball second in Q1 yet first in Q3, shifting scoring between quarters.
Two-minute efficiency interacts with timeout and pace habits to concentrate first-half scoring in the last 2 minutes of Q2.
Halftime lead interacts with script: second-half pace and run rate depend on whether a team is leading by more than a score.

game_total.mechanism: Totals are the product of possessions and points per possession for both teams. Drives depend on pace, run/pass mix and turnover rates; points per drive on opponent-adjusted efficiency, field position, red-zone finishing, kicker range and weather. Both teams' outputs are correlated through game script and environment, so the distribution of total has a fat right tail from blowouts and explosive plays; both-teams-score and team-total markets are slices of the same joint distribution.
game_total.target: Sum of the two teams' points (or each team's points, or whether each team scores at least N) under the contract's regulation/OT settlement.

inputs.why: Plays per game scale all scoring; pace is a stable team trait.
Expected possessions are the base unit of scoring; drive count differs from plays due to turnovers, punts and clock-killing.
Pass-heavy teams stop the clock and sustain pace; PROE sets passing volume and yards.
Offensive EPA per play, opponent-adjusted, anchors points per drive for each team.
Opponent defense efficiency suppresses points per drive and changes the pass/rush split of scoring.
Explosive-play rates raise scoring variance and the fat right tail of the total distribution.
Red-zone TD versus FG conversion changes points per scoring opportunity by up to 4 points per trip and regresses to league mean.
Wind and precipitation lower totals; effects nonlinear.
Kicker range and accuracy determine how many stalled drives convert to 3 points and the key-number structure of totals.
Starter versus backup QB shifts both team points and pace and is only resolved late; total must be a mixture.
Teams scoring above or below their drive-efficiency expectation regress; recent points should be discounted accordingly.
Empirical total residuals and key numbers calibrate rung probabilities.
OT adds points in tied games; inclusion depends on wording.
Sharp totals incorporate weather and lineup information; the Kalshi ladder should be compared to the de-vigged consensus.

interactions.hypothesis: Pace and efficiency are multiplicative: a high-pace offense against a high-pace defense compounds possessions, while two slow, run-heavy teams under-shoot even if efficiency is average.
Wind interacts with explosive passing and kicking: high wind removes deep-pass explosives and long FG, cutting points more for vertical offenses than for run-heavy teams.
Spread size interacts with total: lopsided expected games shift clock-killing run rate for the leader, reducing the favorite's late scoring.

game_event.mechanism: Game-event and stat markets (overtime, safety, both teams score, team stats, TD counts, period TDs) are tails or slices of the underlying drive and score process. They depend on base rates of rare events (overtime, safeties, defensive TDs), the correlation structure of scoring, and team style indicators (pass rush, red-zone play, turnovers) that shift event hazards.
game_event.target: Occurrence or count of a game-level event or team stat (overtime, safety, touchdowns, turnovers, sacks, etc.) under the contract definition.

inputs.why: Margin distribution mass near zero determines overtime probability and tie mass.
OT rules and rate underpin OT-related events.
Event counts scale with plays and drives.
Turnover and takeaway hazards drive event counts such as turnovers or defensive TDs.
Pass-rush strength drives sacks and safeties.
Weak pass blocking raises sack and safety hazard.
Red-zone finishing governs TD counts.
Rare-event base rates conditioned on style.
Penalty-heavy games alter drive counts.
Weather shifts pass rate and thus sacks, turnovers and scoring events.
Expected team scoring is the basis for count markets.
Event definitions (OT inclusion, which team, official scoring) must be matched.

interactions.hypothesis: Close pre-game spread interacts with total to determine overtime probability: tight, low-scoring games with kicker-dependent scoring have more mass on ties.
Pass-rush strength interacts with OL weakness and QB time-to-throw to raise sack, safety and turnover hazards.
Turnover luck interacts with scoring: takeaways produce short fields and drive TD counts, so realized turnover luck should be regressed before using it for event hazards.

first_event.mechanism: First-score and race-to-N markets resolve on the earliest scoring events: opening possession, scripted early plays, red-zone and kicker behaviour, turnovers giving short fields, and overall team scoring rates. The probability that a team scores first is roughly proportional to its share of early scoring hazard, shifted by who has the ball first; timing markets integrate the hazard over play time.
first_event.target: Which team scores first (or reaches N points first) and at what game time, under contract definition of scoring play.

inputs.why: Who receives first shifts first-score probability by several percentage points.
Opening-drive scripts give team-specific first-drive scoring rates.
Efficiency determines hazard of scoring on each possession.
Opposing defense efficiency suppresses hazard.
Faster tempo increases number of plays before a reference time.
Red-zone finish determines TD vs FG for first score type.
FG range and accuracy matter for first-score timing when drives stall.
Expected scoring split by team gives baseline hazards.
Early turnovers create short fields and quick scores.
What counts as scoring (TD, FG, safety) and how ties/no-score resolve.

interactions.hypothesis: Receiving first and scripted opening drive: a team with high opening-drive TD rate and the first possession is much more likely to score first than the average, and the opposite for slow starters.
Kicker range and weather change whether first-score hazard is TD or FG, shifting timing distribution for TD-specific markets.
Pace affects the number of plays available before a time threshold, so high tempo teams have higher early scoring hazard.

player_td.mechanism: Touchdown scorer markets (first, next, anytime) decompose into team TD expectation, player share of scoring opportunities (goal-line carries, red-zone targets, QB sneaks), timing of the first score, and opposing red-zone defense. Because scoring is rare per player and highly role-concentrated, opportunity usage beats realized TD history, and TD luck regresses.
player_td.target: Probability that a named player scores the first/next TD (or any TD) in the game under contract wording on which scores count.

inputs.why: Role-based scoring rate is the core of the player probability.
Red-zone and goal-line shares reveal opportunity concentration.
Team TD expectation sets total scoring pool.
First-drive usage sets first TD probability.
Possession order affects first scoring team.
Goal-line carry share determines rushing TD probability.
End-zone and red-zone targets determine receiving TD probability.
Injuries change shares of teammates.
Realized TD rate regresses; use opportunity not outcomes.
Opposing red-zone defense and position funneling modulate scoring.
Early exit lowers TD probability and shifts volume to others.
Whether defensive/special-teams TDs and 2-pt plays count.

interactions.hypothesis: Team total and personnel share interact: a goal-line back's TD probability rises with team rushing TD expectation but falls if the QB or WR is the preferred red-zone option, so shares must be conditional on formation.
Spread and script interact with goal-line role: trailing teams pass more near the goal line, shifting TD probability from RBs to WR/TE.
Injury to a teammate interacts with target competition to redistribute red-zone looks.

lineup_role.mechanism: Availability and role-event markets resolve on whether a player is active, starts, plays a threshold of snaps or has a specified role; the information chain is practice participation, official designation, coach statements, depth chart and inactive list, each arriving at known times. Probabilities come from calibrating these signals against historical outcomes by position and injury type.
lineup_role.target: Whether a player plays/starts/reaches a role threshold (active status, snap count, starter) as defined by the contract and source.

inputs.why: Timestamped practice status and designation are primary signals.
Inactive list is the definitive pre-game signal.
Starter ordering and role changes.
Beat reporting and coach statements often precede official reports.
Return-from-injury snap limits affect snap-threshold events.
Clinched or eliminated teams rest or limit starters in late-season games, raising the chance a player on the report is Out.
Recent snap share sets role baseline.
Coach history on resting players and use of designations.
Mid-game exit risk affects threshold events.
Market closing relative to report timing defines information set.
Definitions of active, started, played and source determine settlement.

interactions.hypothesis: Practice sequence and designation interact with position: a limited Friday practice with Questionable label implies different play probabilities for QB, RB and OL.
Seeding stakes interact with injury designation: a minor injury plus clinched seed greatly increases rest probability.
Market close time interacts with report timing: before inactives the market must hedge, after inactives it should converge to 0/1.

player_other.mechanism: Player stat markets (yards, receptions, TDs, passing, rushing) are volume times efficiency, where volume comes from team plays, pass/run mix (script) and role share, and efficiency from opponent-adjusted skill, scheme and environment. Ladders over multiple thresholds require a full distribution with variance from role, script, weather and injury exit, and neighbouring rungs are strongly correlated.
player_other.target: Probability that a player's stat (passing/rushing/receiving yards, receptions, completions, TDs) exceeds a threshold (or beats another player), under official stat settlement.

inputs.why: Team pass volume is the base for QB and receiver counting stats.
Plays per game scales opportunity.
Expected game script splits volume between passing and rushing.
Target share and depth determine receiving distributions.
Carry share determines rushing volume.
Quarterback efficiency drives passing and receiver output.
Opponent adjusted position defense.
Coverage shells shape which receivers get targets.
Pressure and time to throw modify passing efficiency.
Wind and rain reduce passing and shift to rushing.
Teammate injuries redistribute volume.
Distribution shape determines ladder probabilities.
Rung consistency and implied distribution.
DNP/void rules and stat source.
Thresholds within a yard or a reception of the line are exposed to post-game stat revisions and source differences.
Realized hit rates by rung calibrate the model and expose systematic over/under-pricing of specific thresholds.

interactions.hypothesis: Spread and pass rate over expected: trailing teams throw more, so for the underdog's QB and WRs volume rises while efficiency falls against softer coverage; favorites run more.
Pressure and time to throw: a quick-release QB behind a poor OL has a low sack and efficiency loss; a slow-release QB suffers more.
